title: Scalable Entanglement Distribution Using Encoded Hybrid Repeater Chains
authors: Stav Haldar, Saikat Guha, Don Towsley, Filip Rozp\k{e}dek
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-distance entanglement distribution requires error correction protocols to compensate for qubit decoherence in quantum memories and noise introduced during entanglement swapping. We argue that repeater chains with error-correction capabilities should exploit more than one physical platform, combining the complementary strengths of different quantum memory technologies into a single hybrid repeater architecture. An important constituent of such an architecture is a hybrid repeater which combines type-1 memories, characterized by fast entanglement generation rates and suitability for multiplexing, and type-2 memories that offer long coherence times and low two-qubit gate error rates. Taking the resource-intensive nature of hybrid nodes into account, we propose and analyze repeater chains in which only a subset of nodes need to be hybrid, while the remaining nodes are simpler first-generation repeaters with no error-correction capability. Through detailed Monte Carlo simulations of fault-tolerant encoded repeater chain protocols based on the three-qubit phase-flip repetition code, the [MATH] Steane code, and the [MATH] Shor code, we demonstrate that these hybrid architectures outperform pure architectures based on a single memory platform in terms of end-to-end entanglement distribution rate. In our study we develop a full circuit-level noise model of our architectures and examine the impact of an imperfect interface between the two platforms on our hybrid architecture. We also develop a modified version of the swap-as-soon-as-possible policy with multiplexing, more suited to our architecture where some nodes perform error-correction while others do not. This modified policy significantly reduces the information storage time in memory qubits relative to the previously considered swap policies in encoded repeater chains.
tldr: The paper proposes hybrid repeater chains that combine fast type-1 memories with long-coherence type-2 memories and error correction to improve end-to-end entanglement distribution rates.
motivation: Long-distance entanglement distribution suffers from decoherence in quantum memories and noise during entanglement swapping, requiring error correction; however, purely single-platform architectures may not optimally balance speed, coherence, and gate fidelity.
method: The authors design repeater chains where only a subset of nodes are hybrid while others are first-generation repeaters, and they perform Monte Carlo simulations of fault-tolerant encoded protocols using three-qubit phase-flip repetition, Steane, and Shor codes under a circuit-level noise model.
result: Hybrid architectures outperform pure single-memory-platform architectures in end-to-end entanglement distribution rate, and a modified swap-as-soon-as-possible policy with multiplexing reduces information storage time in memory qubits.
conclusion: Combining complementary quantum memory platforms in encoded repeater chains is a promising route to scalable entanglement distribution, with benefits persisting under realistic noise and imperfect interfaces.

title: Quantum Tree Networks: Complete Semidefinite Hierarchies And The Source-transfer Model
authors: Xiangling Xu, Igor Klep, Marc-Olivier Renou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the capabilities and limits of quantum systems is central to quantum information processing. This includes determining which correlations can arise in networks of quantum systems distributed by independent sources. Yet for general quantum networks, no systematic, dimension-free method is known to bound these correlations arbitrarily well. We resolve this problem for all quantum tree networks through a new source-transfer model, which we prove equivalent to a mixed quantum model. The mixed model places no restriction on dimension and reduces to the standard tensor-product model in finite dimensions; the source-transfer model instead describes these correlations through states on [MATH]-algebras and completely positive maps composed recursively along the tree. We prove the equivalence by reconstructing local measurements as Radon-Nikodym derivatives in the spatial tensor products prescribed by the network. Building on this characterization, we establish two convergent outer hierarchies of semidefinite programs (SDPs): a novel source-transfer hierarchy and the inflation-NPA hierarchy. For the source-transfer hierarchy, we extend noncommutative real algebraic geometry to multi-state polynomials with completely positive maps, prove a reconstruction theorem establishing its convergence, and give a sufficient stopping criterion for extracting finite-dimensional realizations. For the inflation-NPA hierarchy, we reconstruct source-transfer realizations from weak-operator limits of averages over source copies. Consequently, the game-value promise problem for quantum tree networks in the mixed model is [MATH]-complete.
tldr: The paper introduces a source-transfer model and convergent semidefinite programming hierarchies to completely characterize correlations in all quantum tree networks.
motivation: General quantum networks lack dimension-free methods to bound the correlations achievable with independent sources, limiting our understanding of their capabilities and limits.
method: It proves equivalence between a source-transfer model and a dimension-free mixed quantum model by reconstructing local measurements as Radon-Nikodym derivatives, then builds two convergent outer SDP hierarchies: a novel source-transfer hierarchy extending noncommutative real algebraic geometry, and the inflation-NPA hierarchy.
result: The hierarchies provide arbitrarily tight bounds for quantum tree network correlations, include a stopping criterion for finite-dimensional realizations, and imply that the game-value promise problem for quantum tree networks in the mixed model is complete for a certain complexity class.
conclusion: This resolves the problem of systematically bounding correlations in general quantum tree networks and establishes a powerful SDP-based framework for analyzing network quantum correlations.

title: A Square-Root Barrier To Quantum Gate Speed Under Linear Coupling
authors: Mischa P. Woods Pablo Restrepo Gaviria
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Faster quantum gates can suppress the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors stronger microwave pulses can also increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate parametrically faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that fixed-fidelity gate transition rates grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under stated uniformity conditions on the coupling and accepted dynamics. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.
tldr: The paper proves a square-root energy scaling barrier for quantum gate speed under linear coupling to a bosonic drive field, showing that nonclassical pulse engineering alone cannot achieve linear speed improvements.
motivation: Faster quantum gates can reduce decoherence, but stronger drives in superconducting processors cause leakage, crosstalk, and errors, creating a fundamental energy-speed-error tradeoff that motivates understanding the ultimate limits of pulse-driven gate speed.
method: The authors treat the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field and derive a bound on fixed-fidelity gate transition rates for finite-dimensional systems coupled linearly to the field, allowing arbitrary pulse states, drive-system entanglement, and backaction under uniformity conditions.
result: They prove that the gate transition rate grows at most as the square root of the pulse energy, and that coherent Gaussian pulses saturate this exponent, meaning squeezing or other nonclassical state engineering cannot replace the square-root law.
conclusion: Achieving linear energy scaling for gate speed requires modifying the interaction class, identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.

This bound holds for arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, and allows for drive–system entanglement and back action. title: Experimental Certification Of The Nonlocal Advantages Of Quantum Imaginarity
authors: Jian-Hao Wu, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yun-Xiang Tian, Hao-Ran Tan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, Ya Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum imaginarity is a distinct resource in quantum information theory, yet its nonlocal properties have not been fully explored. Here, we report an experimental study of the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI), in which local measurements on one subsystem can steer the average imaginarity of the conditional states of the other subsystem beyond the corresponding classical bound. The [MATH]-norm of imaginarity inequality is adopted as an experimentally accessible witness. A hybrid optimization algorithm that combines a genetic algorithm with sequential quadratic programming is developed to avoid local optima and accelerate the search for optimal measurement settings. Using polarization-encoded photonic qubits, we prepare two classes of two-qubit Bell-diagonal states and experimentally characterize the imaginarity of the conditional states following local measurements. Clear violations of the [MATH]-norm of imaginarity inequality are observed, providing an experimental certification of NAQI. We further investigate the relationship among NAQI, the nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence (NAQC), and Bell nonlocality based on their respective inequality criteria. For the two-qubit Werner states considered in this work, the regions of states that violate the respective criteria satisfy [MATH]. Our work provides an experimental realization of NAQI and a comparison of different forms of quantum nonclassicality in a photonic platform.
tldr: The paper experimentally certifies the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity using photonic qubits and compares it with quantum coherence and Bell nonlocality.
motivation: Quantum imaginarity is a distinct quantum resource, but its nonlocal properties remain largely unexplored, necessitating an experimental test and comparison with other forms of quantum nonclassicality.
method: Two-qubit Bell-diagonal states are prepared via polarization-encoded photons, local measurements are performed, and a hybrid genetic algorithm combined with sequential quadratic programming optimizes the measurement settings to violate the l1-norm imaginarity inequality.
result: Clear violations of the imaginarity inequality are observed for two classes of Bell-diagonal states, and for Werner states the regions violating NAQI, NAQC, and Bell nonlocality satisfy a specific inclusion relation.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental realization of the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity and a comparative study of different quantum nonclassicality criteria in a photonic platform.

title: A Bi-Objective Routing Framework For Hybrid Terrestrial-Satellite Quantum Networks
authors: Nitish K. Panigrahy Yashpreet Khambay
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid terrestrial-satellite quantum networks combine terrestrial fiber infrastructure with free-space links to enable long-distance entanglement distribution. Entanglement can be routed over different combinations of terrestrial and satellite links, resulting in paths with different entanglement generation rates (EGRs) and fidelities. Existing routing algorithms, however, typically reduce routing to a single-objective problem by optimizing either EGR or fidelity, or by optimizing one while constraining the other, and thus do not explicitly capture the trade-off between the two. In this paper, we present a bi-objective routing framework for hybrid quantum networks that jointly optimizes end-to-end EGR and fidelity. We formulate routing as a Pareto optimization problem and show that it possesses a special mathematical structure: the bottleneck nature of end-to-end EGR and the multiplicative nature of end-to-end fidelity allow the problem to be transformed into a MAXMIN-MINSUM bi-criterion path problem. This transformation enables the exact polynomial-time computation of a minimal complete Pareto set using Martins' bicriterion routing algorithm. Our results demonstrate that hybrid networks expose substantially richer Pareto frontiers than terrestrial-only networks and that the proposed framework outperforms representative single-objective routing policies by allowing applications to select paths based on their EGR and fidelity requirements.
tldr: A bi-objective routing framework for hybrid terrestrial-satellite quantum networks that jointly optimizes entanglement generation rate and fidelity via Pareto optimization.
motivation: Existing routing algorithms for quantum networks typically reduce routing to a single objective, optimizing either entanglement generation rate (EGR) or fidelity, or constraining one while optimizing the other, thereby failing to capture the inherent trade-off.
method: The problem is formulated as a Pareto optimization and shown to reduce to a MAXMIN-MINSUM bi-criterion path problem due to the bottleneck nature of EGR and multiplicative nature of fidelity; Martins' bicriterion routing algorithm is then used to compute the exact minimal complete Pareto set in polynomial time.
result: Hybrid terrestrial-satellite networks exhibit substantially richer Pareto frontiers than terrestrial-only networks, and the proposed framework outperforms representative single-objective routing policies by allowing applications to select paths based on their EGR and fidelity requirements.
conclusion: The bi-objective framework provides a principled and efficient approach for entanglement routing in hybrid quantum networks, enabling application-specific path selection that balances rate and fidelity.

The paper reports that hybrid networks expose substantially richer Pareto frontiers than terrestrial-only networks, and that the framework outperforms representative single-objective routing policies by letting applications select paths according to their EGR and fidelity requirements.

title: Contact Large Deviations Of Stochastic Vector Bundles
authors: D. Y. Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large deviation theory lacks a geometric foundation for its rate functions and fluctuation symmetries. This paper develops a contact large deviation theory on stochastic vector bundles, in which the rate function, the scaled cumulant generating function, and a Gallavotti--Cohen-type fluctuation duality all follow from the contact 1-form. The constraint function acts as a generalized Lagrangian; the least constraint principle yields the dynamics, and the contact potential is built order by order from the master equation, producing a coupled Hamilton--Jacobi--transport system governed by the invariant density, drift, and fluctuation tensor. The contact path measure satisfies a large deviation principle with rate function given by the constraint action; the scaled cumulant generating function obeys a stationary eigenvalue equation with a Donsker--Varadhan variational characterization. The entropy production rate, the fluctuation--dissipation combination [MATH], is the physical observable; the time-reversal involution [MATH] with reversed drift [MATH] yields a Gallavotti--Cohen-type duality [MATH]. The classical one-dimensional GC symmetry is recovered in the reversible case [MATH].

title: Achieving The Limits Of Automorphism Gates
authors: Jin Ming Koh, Shayan Majidy, Aranya Chakraborty, Anqi Gong, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Norman Y. Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universal fault-tolerant quantum computing combines versatile but expensive operations with specialized but cheap ones. Its efficiency depends on how much computation can be pushed onto the cheap operations and on the size of the code needed to do so. Automorphism gates provide such cheap operations using only physical single-qubit Clifford gates and qubit permutations. Yet no general theory characterizes their maximum logical power or the minimum code size needed to attain it. We develop such a theory. For stabilizer codes encoding [MATH] logical qubits, we show that the largest logical group attainable by automorphisms is generated by all addressable [MATH] and [MATH] gates, and we construct codes attaining it. While this group contains exponentially fewer gates than the full Clifford group, adding one suitable non-Clifford gate yields universality. We further classify the largest logical groups attainable using qubit permutations, physical single-qubit Cliffords, or both across general stabilizer and CSS codes, and derive refined bounds for self-dual CSS subclasses. Achieving the maximum-size logical group through automorphisms requires [MATH] physical qubits. By contrast, all addressable diagonal Clifford gates, generated by [MATH] and [MATH], require only [MATH] physical qubits when implemented using physical single-qubit Cliffords alone. Both bounds are tight. This polynomial qubit cost extends beyond Cliffords to all addressable diagonal gates at any fixed level of the Clifford hierarchy, using physical single-qubit diagonal gates. Thus, for full addressability, the sharpest physical-qubit cost divide lies between diagonal and [MATH]-type gates, not between Clifford and non-Clifford gates.

title: Theory Of Post-selected Entanglement Transitions In Monitored Bosons
authors: Ilia Komissarov, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre, Ahana Chakraborty
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement phase transitions driven by quantum measurements have emerged as a central paradigm in open quantum many-body physics. Such phase transitions are well established for systems with finite local Hilbert-space dimensions, such as qubits and fermions, while their realization in bosonic systems with unbounded local occupation numbers remains poorly understood. Even in the absence of interactions, number states of bosons are intrinsically non-Gaussian, preventing the use of standard correlation-matrix approaches. To address this problem, we develop a replica-free Keldysh field-theoretic framework that expresses the Renyi entropy of bosonic systems initialized in on-site Fock states in terms of permanents of matrices constructed from single-particle Green's functions. Applying this framework to a continuously monitored one-dimensional cross-stitch lattice conditioned on the no-click trajectory, we uncover a transition from volume-law to logarithmic entanglement scaling. We show that the transition is controlled by a restructuring of the non-Hermitian spectrum that changes the number of long-lived modes from extensive to finite. In the strongly monitored regime, bosons dynamically condense into a microscopic number of slowest-decaying modes, producing logarithmic entanglement scaling, whereas an extensive manifold of long-lived modes at weak monitoring gives rise to volume-law entanglement. Our results establish a distinct mechanism for measurement-induced entanglement transitions in free bosonic systems and provide a computationally efficient diagnostic of the measurement-induced bosonic condensation.

motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement transitions are well established for finite-dimensional systems, but bosonic systems with unbounded local occupation remain poorly understood because number states are non-Gaussian and correlation-matrix methods fail.
method: The authors introduce a Keldysh field-theoretic framework that expresses Renyi entropy for on-site Fock initial states as permanents of matrices built from single-particle Green's functions, and apply it to a continuously monitored one-dimensional cross-stitch lattice under the no-click trajectory.
result: They find a transition from volume-law to logarithmic entanglement scaling, governed by a change in the number of long-lived non-Hermitian modes from extensive to finite; strong monitoring induces dynamical condensation into a few slowest-decaying modes.
conclusion: The work establishes a distinct mechanism for measurement-induced entanglement transitions in free bosonic systems and provides a computationally efficient diagnostic of measurement-induced bosonic condensation.

title: Emergent Classicality And Wavefunction Branching In An Isolated Quantum Many-body System
authors: Sa\'ul Pilatowsky-Cameo, Jordan Cotler, Daniel Ranard, C. Jess Riedel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoherence in quantum systems is conventionally modeled as the effect of interactions with an external environment. However, such a prescription excludes isolated many-body systems, which are also expected to display classical behavior at macroscopic scales. In isolated systems, decoherence must emerge internally from microscopic degrees of freedom that are invisible to the macroscopic description. Here we explicitly show that classicality can emerge in such a fashion. We consider a weakly disordered, [MATH]-local chaotic kicked top of [MATH] qubits, where the collective spin sector serves as the macroscopic description, while the microscopic permutation sector acts as an internal bath, decohering the collective spin sector. Starting from closed unitary dynamics, we derive and numerically confirm an effective Lindblad equation for the collective spin variables. In the thermodynamic limit these reduced dynamics converge to a classical chaotic Fokker--Planck equation with vanishingly small diffusion on the spherical phase space, producing a quantum-classical correspondence beyond the Ehrenfest time. The chaotic dynamics evolve the pure many-body wavefunction into continuously branching components associated with distinct classical trajectories. These branches acquire nearly orthogonal microscopic records in the permutation sector, preventing quantum interferences and ensuring the corresponding histories remain consistent.
tldr: The paper shows that classicality can emerge in an isolated chaotic many-body system via internal decoherence, with the collective spin sector obeying an effective Lindblad equation and converging to classical Fokker-Planck dynamics.
motivation: Decoherence is usually attributed to an external environment, but isolated many-body systems are also expected to display classical behavior, so an internal mechanism for decoherence is needed.
method: The authors study a weakly disordered k-local chaotic kicked top of qubits, treating the collective spin as the macroscopic sector and the permutation sector as an internal bath, and derive and numerically confirm an effective Lindblad equation for the collective variables.
result: In the thermodynamic limit, the reduced dynamics converge to a classical chaotic Fokker-Planck equation with vanishing diffusion, producing quantum-classical correspondence beyond the Ehrenfest time, while the pure wavefunction branches into components with nearly orthogonal microscopic records.
conclusion: Classicality and consistent histories can arise in isolated quantum many-body systems through internal microscopic degrees of freedom, without an external environment.

They study a weakly disordered, 3-local chaotic kicked top model of N qubits, where the collective spin sector represents the macroscopic observable, and the permutation sector (associated with the symmetric group) acts as an internal bath. Starting from closed unitary dynamics, they derive an effective Lindblad master equation for the collective spin variables by tracing out the permutation sector, and numerically confirm its validity. In the thermodynamic limit, the reduced dynamics converge to a classical chaotic Fokker-Planck equation on the spherical phase space with vanishingly small diffusion. This yields a quantum-classical correspondence that persists beyond the Ehrenfest time. The chaotic dynamics cause the pure many-body wavefunction to branch into components following distinct classical trajectories; these branches acquire nearly orthogonal records in the permutation sector, which suppress quantum interference and enforce consistent histories.

By separating the Hilbert space into a collective spin sector (macroscopic) and a permutation sector (microscopic), they trace out the permutation degrees of freedom to obtain an effective Lindblad master equation for the collective spin. This derivation likely uses projection operator techniques or cumulant expansions, assuming that the permutation sector acts as a Markovian bath. The numerical confirmation involves exact diagonalization or matrix product state simulations for small N to validate the Lindblad equation. They then take the thermodynamic limit (N → ∞) to map the Lindblad dynamics onto a classical Fokker-Planck equation on the sphere, with diffusion coefficient scaling inversely with N. The analysis of branching and records uses concepts from quantum trajectories and consistent histories.

In the thermodynamic limit, the Lindblad equation reduces to a classical Fokker-Planck equation with a diffusion term that vanishes as 1/N, leading to deterministic classical chaotic dynamics on the sphere. This implies that the quantum-classical correspondence holds beyond the Ehrenfest time, which is typically limited by decoherence. The branching of the wavefunction into multiple components is quantified by the growth of entanglement between the collective and permutation sectors, with the permutation sector recording which classical trajectory is followed. title: Efficiently Estimating Failure Rates Of Fault-tolerant Logical non-Clifford Blocks
authors: Thomas R. Scruby Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Useful quantum computation requires the fault-tolerant implementations of a universal gate set which are generically not efficiently simulable. We devise an algebraic framework that allows for efficient sampling from the measurement distribution of fault-tolerant circuits that implement diagonal logic gates in the third level of the Clifford hierarchy. Upon successful sampling we also provide sufficient conditions for decoding success. The resulting estimate for the logical failure rate is an overestimate, which becomes more accurate for blocks that are fault tolerant against arbitrary local errors. The non-Clifford simulation overhead is independent of the number of logical qubits, making the method particularly attractive for large-scale simulations. The framework is based on viewing the non-Clifford gates in the circuit as a cohomology invariant of an underlying spacetime fault complex. The method can also be interfaced with Clifford simulators to simulate larger fault-tolerant circuits and algorithmic subroutines.
tldr: The paper develops an algebraic framework to efficiently estimate logical failure rates of fault-tolerant non-Clifford blocks by sampling measurement distributions and checking decoding success.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computation requires reliable non-Clifford gates, but their classical simulation is generically inefficient, making failure-rate estimation hard.
method: The authors view non-Clifford gates as cohomology invariants of an underlying spacetime fault complex, enabling efficient sampling from measurement distributions of diagonal gates in the third level of the Clifford hierarchy and providing sufficient conditions for decoding success.
result: The estimated logical failure rate is an overestimate that becomes more accurate for blocks fault-tolerant against arbitrary local errors, with non-Clifford simulation overhead independent of the number of logical qubits and compatible with Clifford simulators.
conclusion: This framework enables efficient estimation of failure rates for large-scale fault-tolerant non-Clifford blocks and algorithmic subroutines, aiding the design of universal fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Fifty Years Of The Gkls Master Equation: Foundations And Early Developments
authors: Fabio Benatti, Dariusz Chru\'sci\'nski, Saverio Pascazio
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The year 2026 marks the fiftieth anniversary of the two seminal papers in which Gorini, Kossakowski, and Sudarshan, and independently Lindblad, characterized the generators of completely positive quantum dynamical semigroups. We revisit the conceptual and historical route leading to the Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation and examine several of its early developments and consequences. Our aim is to show how several initially separate mathematical and physical ideas converged in the GKLS structure theorem, imme- diately opening the way to manifold consequences for the description of dissipative quantum phenomena and how that theorem, fifty years later, remains both a foundational result and an active framework for open quantum dynamics.
tldr: A historical and conceptual review of the Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation on its fiftieth anniversary, tracing the ideas that converged into the structure theorem for completely positive quantum dynamical semigroups and surveying its early consequences for dissipative quantum dynamics.
motivation: The 50th anniversary of the two 1976 seminal papers by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan and Lindblad provides an occasion to reconstruct how separate mathematical and physical threads merged into the GKLS characterization of Markovian quantum dynamics.
method: Conceptual and historical review, revisiting primary literature and the mathematical/physical arguments leading to the GKLS structure theorem, together with a survey of its early developments and applications.
result: The paper shows how the independent mathematical and physical strands converged into a single foundational theorem and illustrates the manifold consequences it opened up for describing dissipative quantum phenomena.
conclusion: Fifty years on, the GKLS theorem remains both a foundational result and an active framework for open quantum dynamics, making this retrospective a useful reference for the field.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper is a historical and conceptual review commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKLS) master equation, published in a special volume of OSID. The authors trace the intellectual lineage of the GKLS theorem, which characterizes the generators of completely positive quantum dynamical semigroups, from early mathematical developments in functional analysis and semigroup theory to the physical motivations from quantum statistical mechanics and open quantum systems. They emphasize how disparate ideas—such as Stinespring's dilation theorem, the Hille-Yosida theorem, and the notion of complete positivity—converged to yield the now-canonical form of the Markovian master equation. The paper then surveys several early consequences and applications of the GKLS structure, including the classification of generators, the role of the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators, and the emergence of dissipative phenomena like decoherence and relaxation. It concludes by reflecting on the enduring impact of the GKLS equation as both a foundational result and a practical tool in modern quantum physics, highlighting its continued relevance in fields ranging from quantum optics to quantum information science.

Surveys early and influential applications of the GKLS equation, demonstrating its role in describing dissipative quantum phenomena such as decoherence, relaxation, and approach to equilibrium.

The authors synthesize primary literature from the 1960s and 1970s, including the original papers by Gorini, Kossakowski, and Sudarshan (1976) and Lindblad (1976), alongside related works on semigroups, complete positivity, and quantum dynamical maps. They adopt a chronological and thematic structure, tracing the evolution of ideas from early mathematical abstractions to physical applications. The analysis is qualitative, focusing on the logical connections between concepts and the interpretation of key theorems. It reiterates the central result: any generator L of a completely positive, trace-preserving semigroup on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space can be written in the GKLS form: L(ρ) = -i[H, ρ] + Σ_k (L_k ρ L_k† - 1/2 {L_k† L_k, ρ}). The authors discuss the significance of the Lindblad operators L_k and the Hamiltonian H, and how the structure ensures complete positivity and trace preservation. abstract: ArXiv:2609.19317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous quantum displacement measurements are fundamentally limited by a trade-off between readout imprecision and measurement back-action, constrained by the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. In the Laser Interferometric Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO), these two quantum noise components dominate much of the observation band, making it an excellent testbed. We induce a sub-Hz-linewidth optomechanical mode by trapping the differential motion of the 40-kg mirrors in a band where radiation-pressure back-action dominates the motion. Engineering the quantum state entering the dark port creates correlations between imprecision and back-action that partially cancel their contributions, reducing observed motion near resonance by ~47%. A framework resolving the imprecision, back-action, and correlation terms identifies the origin of this suppression. These results demonstrate quantum back-action evasion and quantum reservoir engineering in a macroscopic optomechanical system.

title: Universal Suppression Of Dissipation Across Conformal Interface In Open Quantum Critical Systems
authors: Ruhanshi Barad, Tian Wu, Qicheng Tang, Xueda Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conformal interfaces provide an important setting for studying universal transmission phenomena in one-dimensional quantum critical systems. While energy and information transmission across such interfaces are characterized by universal quantities in closed systems, the corresponding role of conformal interfaces in dissipative dynamics is less understood. In this work, we study relaxation in locally dissipative quantum critical chains with a conformal interface and show that a universal characterization emerges at the level of individual relaxation modes. We first show that the relaxation coefficient defined in the recent work [1] from the Liouvillian gap can become non-universal for certain boundary conditions because the mode determining the smallest decay rate can change as the interface transmission is varied. To resolve this ambiguity, we introduce a mode-resolved relaxation coefficient [MATH] by continuously tracking the same Liouvillian rapidity mode as a function of the interface transmission. Using analytical and numerical calculations for a critical harmonic chain and a critical free-fermion chain, we find that, in the weak-dissipation regime, [MATH] follows the same universal dependence on the interface transmission in all cases considered, independent of microscopic details such as the boundary conditions, dissipation strength, and location of the local dissipation. For boundary dissipation, this universal behavior persists even at finite dissipation strength. Our results establish a universal mode-resolved characterization of relaxation across conformal interfaces in open quantum critical systems.

motivation: Conformal interfaces govern universal transmission in closed critical systems, but their role in dissipative open-system dynamics remains poorly understood.
method: Using analytical and numerical methods for a critical harmonic chain and a critical free-fermion chain, the authors track individual Liouvillian rapidity modes as a function of interface transmission under weak dissipation.

conclusion: The results establish a universal mode-resolved characterization of relaxation across conformal interfaces in open quantum critical systems.

title: Holomorphic Quantum Error Correction Codes
authors: M. W. Almasri
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a holomorphic representation of quantum error correction codes (QECCs) within the Segal--Bargmann space. By encoding qubits into Schwinger boson modes [MATH] subject to a degree-one homogeneity constraint, we derive closed-form differential operator representations for stabilizers, syndrome extraction, and recovery for fundamental codes (three-, five-, seven-, and nine-qubit codes). Quantum errors are characterized as holomorphic perturbations violating this constraint, while syndrome measurement projects onto eigenspaces of commuting differential operators. Restricting to unit-magnitude variables ([MATH]) reveals a toroidal space [MATH] where error syndromes manifest as discrete translations in winding number space [MATH], and recovery acts as Hamiltonian flows restoring the winding configuration. In the full Segal--Bargmann space, the code space is a holomorphic submanifold of [MATH], with correctable errors as transverse normal directions. Consequently, the Knill--Laflamme condition becomes a Fubini--Study orthogonality condition between the code submanifold and its error-translated images. Topological protection emerges from the [MATH] fiber bundle structure: global phase noise along fibers is unobservable, while base-space errors require active correction. Finally, we establish a path-integral formulation for semiclassical error correction dynamics and show that geometric entanglement via the Segre embedding naturally quantifies code distance. This framework unifies algebraic, geometric, and topological perspectives on fault-tolerant quantum protocols.

title: Engineering And Probing A One-Dimensional Dipolar Spin Ensemble In Diamond
authors: Lingjie Chen, Shreyas Parthasarathy, Simon A. Meynell, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Eveline Postelnicu, Haopu Yang, Zilin Wang, Weijie Wu, Winston V. Peloso, Casey K. Kim, Chris R. Laumann, Kunal Mukherjee, Norman Y. Yao, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dimensionality plays a central role in determining the collective behavior of interacting quantum systems. Engineering strongly interacting ensembles of solid-state spin defects in reduced dimensions remains a significant challenge at the interface between the applied and fundamental sciences. Here, we create and characterize a positionally disordered, quasi-one-dimensional spin chain in diamond, consisting of optically dark substitutional nitrogen defects (P1 centers) and optically addressable probe nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. Our approach exploits the preferential incorporation of nitrogen along step bunches formed during chemical vapor deposition to achieve both lateral and vertical confinement. Combining spatially resolved materials characterization with nanoscale quantum sensing, we establish the one-dimensional character of the optically dark, unpolarized P1 spin ensemble. We then use correlation spectroscopy to probe local spin autocorrelations and investigate infinite-temperature dipolar spin transport. Our results establish a materials-based route for engineering low-dimensional quantum spin systems.
tldr: The authors engineer and characterize a quasi-one-dimensional chain of dipolar-coupled P1 electron spins in diamond, using NV centers as nanoscale quantum probes of spin autocorrelations and infinite-temperature dipolar transport.

title: Symmetry-driven Correlation Patterns In One-dimensional Periodic Fermionic Systems: Closed-form Expressions And Exact Selection Rules For Correlation Functions, Entanglement Entropies And Mutual Information
authors: Celestino Angeli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analytical study of the spatial structure of correlations in periodic fermionic systems at the single Slater determinant level, focusing on the cyclic case. Exploiting cyclic symmetry, the transformation from localized orbitals to molecular orbitals is simultaneously a discrete Fourier transform, a Vandermonde matrix on the roots of unity, a complex Hadamard matrix, and the character table of the cyclic group [MATH]. Within this framework, the spatial structure of correlations is fully determined by the occupied irreducible representations (Fourier modes), independently of the specific Hamiltonian generating them. In particular, the fermionic two-point correlator is expressed as a truncated Fourier sum over the occupied orbitals, leading to exact analytical expressions for symmetric occupation patterns of Fourier modes ([MATH] and [MATH] pairs), corresponding in quantum chemistry to aromatic fillings, i.e. fillings satisfying H\"uckel's [MATH] rule. For the half filling case, we derive exact spatial selection rules. In particular, the two-point correlator vanishes identically for all even distances along the ring. This property propagates to reduced density matrices and implies a complete absence of mutual information between the corresponding orbitals. These results reveal that, despite the global delocalization of molecular orbitals, the correlation structure in cyclic systems is highly non-uniform and governed by symmetry-induced interference. Although formulated in terms of cyclic lattice systems, the present results extend straightforwardly to one-dimensional fermionic chains with periodic conditions, reflecting the underlying translational symmetry of the problem. The framework therefore provides a Hamiltonian-independent and universal reference for understanding correlation patterns in one-dimensional periodic fermionic systems.
tldr: Analytical study of correlation patterns, entanglement entropies, and mutual information in one-dimensional periodic fermionic systems, deriving exact selection rules from cyclic symmetry.
motivation: To understand how global delocalization of molecular orbitals affects spatial correlation structure and entanglement in periodic fermionic systems, independent of the specific Hamiltonian.
method: Uses Slater determinant formalism, discrete Fourier transform on the cyclic group, and symmetry analysis to express two-point correlators as truncated Fourier sums and derive exact expressions for entanglement entropies and mutual information.
result: At half filling, the two-point correlator vanishes identically for all even distances along the ring, leading to exact selection rules and complete absence of mutual information between certain orbitals for aromatic fillings.
conclusion: The correlation structure is highly non-uniform and governed by symmetry-induced interference, providing a universal Hamiltonian-independent reference for periodic fermionic systems and extending to one-dimensional chains with periodic boundary conditions.

title: Conflict-Free Color-Clustered Sequential Belief-Propagation Decoding Of Quantum Ldpc Codes Via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Mohsen Moradi, Taejoon Kim, Remi A. Chou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief-propagation (BP) decoding for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes is attractive due to its low complexity and low latency, but it is often limited by short cycles, degeneracy, and convergence failures. Reinforcement-learning-based sequential BP decoding (RL-S) improves BP by learning a syndrome-dependent variable-node (VN) update order, but its VN-by-VN schedule has limited within-iteration parallelism. In this paper, we propose a conflict-free color-clustered extension of RL-S. We construct a VN conflict graph in which two VNs are adjacent if they share an X-type or Z-type check, and color this graph so that same-color VNs have disjoint check neighborhoods. This also prevents VNs from the same Tanner 4- or 6-cycle from being updated simultaneously. During decoding, the trained VN-level Q-table selects a seed VN, and all remaining VNs with the same color are updated in parallel using the same pre-batch messages. For the [[288,12,18]] bivariate-bicycle code over the depolarizing channel, our proposed decoder achieves block-error-rate performance close to VN-level RL-S while reducing the scheduling decisions from 288 VNs to 11 color classes per BP iteration.
tldr: A reinforcement-learning-based sequential belief-propagation decoder for quantum LDPC codes is extended with conflict-free color clustering to enable parallel variable-node updates.
motivation: BP decoding of QLDPC codes is attractive for low complexity and latency but suffers from short cycles, degeneracy, and convergence failures; existing RL-S scheduling is limited by VN-by-VN sequential updates.
method: The authors construct a VN conflict graph where VNs sharing X-type or Z-type checks are adjacent, color it so same-color VNs have disjoint check neighborhoods, and use a trained VN-level Q-table to select a seed VN while updating all same-color VNs in parallel.
result: For the [[288,12,18]] bivariate-bicycle code over the depolarizing channel, the proposed decoder achieves block-error-rate performance close to VN-level RL-S while reducing scheduling decisions from 288 VNs to 11 color classes per BP iteration.
conclusion: The conflict-free color-clustered RL-S decoder improves within-iteration parallelism of quantum LDPC BP decoding without significantly sacrificing error-rate performance.

The authors propose a conflict-free color-clustered extension that groups VNs into independent sets based on a conflict graph where two VNs are adjacent if they share an X-type or Z-type check. By coloring this graph, same-color VNs have disjoint check neighborhoods, ensuring that no two VNs in the same Tanner 4- or 6-cycle are updated simultaneously. During decoding, a trained VN-level Q-table selects a seed VN, and all remaining VNs of the same color are updated in parallel using the same pre-batch messages. title: Enhanced Emission And Two-Photon Interference Of Lead-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Solid Immersion Lenses
authors: Koyo Hirai, Eiki Ota, Yiyang Chen, Ren Kato, Peng Wang, Toshiharu Makino, Takashi Taniguchi, Masashi Miyakawa, Shinobu Onoda, Mutsuko Hatano, Takayuki Iwasaki
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A negatively charged lead-vacancy (PbV-) center in diamond is a novel quantum system which can be operated at a high temperature above 4 K owing to its large ground state splitting. To unlock the quantum properties of the PbV- center, the enhancement of the fluorescence intensity is a key issue. Here, we demonstrate enhanced emission from PbV- centers by a factor of approximately 10 using solid immersion lenses (SILs) fabricated on rough diamond surface caused by high-temperature anneal over 2000{\deg}C. Resonant excitation reveals the narrow emission close to the transform-limited linewidth. Furthermore, we demonstrate two-photon interference using one single PbV- center in an SIL. This enhanced emission and indistinguishability will lead to further development of the PbV- center towards quantum network node applications.
tldr: Solid immersion lenses fabricated on annealed diamond enhance PbV- center emission ~10x and enable two-photon interference from a single center, advancing lead-vacancy defects toward quantum network node applications.
motivation: The negatively charged lead-vacancy center in diamond is a promising high-temperature (>4 K) quantum emitter, but its weak fluorescence and optical indistinguishability must be improved before it can serve as a practical node in quantum networks.
method: Solid immersion lenses were patterned on rough diamond surfaces produced by high-temperature annealing above 2000 °C, and the PbV- centers were characterized under resonant excitation, followed by Hong-Ou-Mandel-type two-photon interference measurements.
result: Emission was enhanced by roughly a factor of 10, resonant excitation revealed narrow lines close to the transform limit, and two-photon interference was observed from a single PbV- center inside an SIL.
conclusion: The combination of enhanced collection efficiency and photon indistinguishability positions PbV- centers as viable building blocks for quantum network nodes, motivating further development of this colour-centre platform.

title: Scalable Simulation Of Quantum Dynamics On Topological Quantum Hardware
authors: Mark E. Tuckerman Kritanjan Polley
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computers offer a significant advantage in simulating quantum systems compared to classical computers for certain problems, although most current applications are limited to calculating static molecular properties using hybrid quantum-classical hardware. In this work, we establish a framework for the representation of quantum dynamics in molecular and condensed matter systems, designed for execution on topological quantum hardware. By leveraging the non-Abelian braiding statistics of Fibonacci and Ising anyons, we utilize the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm to approximate unitary propagators for a range of systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of these algorithms across a hierarchy of complexity, from two-level systems and one dimensional double-well potentials to condensed phase spin-boson models, simple molecules, and molecular reaction kinetics. These algorithms provide a scalable and robust pathway for simulating many-body condensed phase chemical physics on fault-tolerant quantum devices.

motivation: Classical simulation of quantum dynamics is challenging due to exponential resource requirements, motivating the use of quantum hardware for efficient simulation.

title: Dephasing-Enhanced Response And Phase Transitions In Quantum Boltzmann Samplers
authors: Yu-Xuan Zhang, Jing-Ling Chen, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Peng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dephasing can drive a quantum Boltzmann sampler into an ordered phase while its programmed probability distribution remains disordered. We trace this transition to an enhanced conditional response: coherence loss changes how each spin responds to its neighbors, and interactions amplify the change. For all-to-all coupling, we establish the stationary transition at finite dephasing. Near criticality, the magnetization distribution depends on the ratio of dephasing strength to the square root of system size, retaining a finite imprint of coherence even as the local coherent correction vanishes. In the strong-dephasing limit on a square lattice, the dynamics generates effective multispin interactions and probability currents, with Ising-like critical statistics. Adjusting the local dissipative update restores the target probability process on arbitrary graphs.
tldr: Dephasing can drive a quantum Boltzmann sampler into an ordered phase even when its programmed probability distribution remains disordered, with a finite-dephasing transition and Ising-like critical statistics.
motivation: Quantum Boltzmann samplers are promising for probabilistic computing, but the effect of environmental dephasing on their stationary state and sampling accuracy is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the open-system dynamics of a quantum Boltzmann sampler with all-to-all and square-lattice couplings, studying the stationary state, conditional response, and critical behavior under dephasing.

title: Temporal Information Processing On A 4,500-qubit Quantum Annealer
authors: Antonio Sannia, Roberto Menta, Pratik Sathe, Dario de Santis, Vittorio Giovannetti, Luis Pedro Garc\'ia-Pintos, Davide Venturelli, Gian Luca Giorgi, Roberta Zambrini, Francesco Caravelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum machine learning could uncover statistical structure beyond the reach of classical models, but this requires quantum models large and expressive enough to be useful and cheap enough to read out. Most approaches optimize many quantum parameters and are thus limited by expensive training loops. Here we report a quantum machine-learning model implemented on a programmable superconducting quantum annealer that processes temporal data at large scale using up to 4,500 qubits-the largest quantum machine-learning experiment performed to date. Following the quantum reservoir computing paradigm, the untrained native many-body dynamics generated by reverse annealing is directly used to process temporal data. We prove that the interactions produced during annealing are indispensable-a non-interacting reservoir retains no memory of its input. We evaluate our model experimentally on standard memory benchmarks and demonstrate that it can successfully forecast chaotic time series. These results establish quantum annealers as a scalable platform for large-scale quantum machine learning.
tldr: A 4,500-qubit superconducting quantum annealer is used as an untrained quantum reservoir to process temporal data, achieving memory benchmarks and chaotic time-series forecasting.
motivation: Quantum machine learning requires large, expressive models that are cheap to read out, but most approaches are limited by expensive training loops.
method: The native many-body dynamics generated by reverse annealing are used directly as a quantum reservoir; the authors prove that interactions are necessary for memory and evaluate performance on memory benchmarks and chaotic time series.
result: The experiment uses up to 4,500 qubits, the largest quantum machine-learning demonstration to date, and shows that a non-interacting reservoir retains no memory while the interacting reservoir successfully forecasts chaotic time series.
conclusion: Quantum annealers can serve as scalable platforms for large-scale quantum machine learning and temporal information processing.

title: Linear Combination Of Schr\"odingerization For Quantum Linear Systems With Optimal Matrix-query Complexity
authors: Yin Yang, Yue Yu, Long Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum linear systems algorithms (QLSAs) aim to solve linear systems [MATH] exponentially faster than classical methods under certain conditions. In this work, we develop quantum algorithms for solving linear algebraic equations from an ODE-based perspective. Inspired by the linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) representation in the Fourier approach , we express the solution [MATH] as a linear combination of solutions to a system of linear convection equations, which become Schr\"odinger-type equations with unitary evolutions in the Fourier domain. We refer to this representation as LC-Schr\"odingerization. Based on this result, we construct an LCHS-based quantum algorithm with two LCHS instances: one for time-marching and one for numerical integration. The key construction uses the derivative of a Gaussian-smoothed hat function and recovers the solution over a fixed auxiliary interval. This permits a truncation time independent of the target accuracy and avoids the loss in success probability from selecting a single grid point. Periodization and explicit Fourier coefficients provide the corresponding projection error bounds. Under the stated oracle assumptions and given a constant-factor estimate of the solution norm, direct simulation of the select operators and block preconditioning achieve the optimal matrix-query complexity [MATH] without using variable-time amplitude amplification (VTAA). The same upper bound holds for queries to the right-hand-side preparation oracle.
tldr: Develops an ODE-based quantum algorithm for linear systems using an LC-Schrödingerization framework to achieve optimal matrix-query complexity without variable-time amplitude amplification.
motivation: Quantum linear systems algorithms promise exponential speedup, but existing methods often suffer from suboptimal query complexity or require variable-time amplitude amplification, motivating new approaches with optimal complexity.
method: The solution is expressed as a linear combination of solutions to linear convection equations that become Schrödinger-type unitary evolutions in the Fourier domain; an LCHS-based algorithm is constructed using time-marching and numerical integration, with a Gaussian-smoothed hat function, periodization, explicit Fourier coefficients, and block preconditioning.
result: The algorithm achieves optimal matrix-query complexity without using variable-time amplitude amplification, and the same upper bound holds for queries to the right-hand-side preparation oracle.
conclusion: This provides a new ODE-inspired route to quantum linear systems with optimal query complexity, potentially broadening algorithmic frameworks for quantum linear algebra.

title: Exact Local Optimality Does Not Compose: The Complexity Of Chronological Realization
authors: Yixin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The chronological shared realization complexity (CRC) is the smallest normalized stochastic state dimension [MATH] needed to reproduce a collection of future-response menus using one shared family of controlled transition dynamics. We focus on the rank-tight regime in which both the local realization dimension and the independent-query static carrier width equal [MATH], thereby isolating the additional dimensional and computational constraints imposed by chronological consistency. This framework also serves as the classical baseline for state-dimension bounds in sequential quantum processes, where stochastic dynamics generalize to completely positive maps. We establish three results in this regime. First, an explicit payload--delay family exhibits an unbounded multiplicative state blow-up: [MATH] while [MATH], isolating the intrinsic state cost of shared temporal pullbacks. Second, for explicitly listed rational finite menus over a fixed five-letter alphabet with a single Boolean terminal effect, exact shared realizability is [MATH]-complete, and the zero-versus-inverse-polynomial defect promise problem is [MATH]-complete, with local and static optima fixed at [MATH]. Third, a total five-letter chronology compiler translates bounded-rational Intermediate Simplex instances into a polynomially specified regular geometric family over the same fixed alphabet, preserving exact local and static width [MATH]. The compiled family yields strong [MATH]-hardness for shared realization on strongly bounded-rational inputs, together with an [MATH] upper bound certified by an exact polynomial-size finite core. Together, these results show that exact local and static optimality need not compose under chronological sharing, even in the rank-tight regime.
tldr: The paper studies chronological shared realization complexity (CRC) and shows that exact local and static optimality does not compose under chronological sharing, establishing NP-completeness and state-blow-up results even in a rank-tight regime.
motivation: To isolate the additional dimensional and computational constraints imposed by chronological consistency in shared stochastic realization, and to provide a classical baseline for state-dimension bounds in sequential quantum processes.
method: Defines the rank-tight regime, constructs a payload-delay family to demonstrate unbounded multiplicative state blow-up, proves NP-completeness for exact shared realizability and a defect promise problem, and introduces a chronology compiler from bounded-rational Intermediate Simplex instances to regular geometric families.
result: Shows an explicit payload-delay family with unbounded multiplicative state blow-up, proves that exact shared realizability over a fixed five-letter alphabet is NP-complete, and obtains strong NP-hardness with a polynomial-size finite core upper bound for bounded-rational inputs.
conclusion: Exact local and static optimality need not compose under chronological sharing, and the framework reveals inherent complexity barriers for shared realization even in the rank-tight regime.

title: A Restricted Boltzmann Machine With Quantum-State Visible Units
authors: Zhe-Hao Zhang, Yi-Cong Yu, Xiaoming Cai, Hai-Qing Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) whose visible input is a quantum state rather than a classical configuration. Each hidden unit carries a trainable quantum template prepared by a parametrized circuit and converts its overlap with the input into a feature. Treating quantum states as high-dimensional continuous visible objects creates nontrivial normalization and scaling problems. We regularize the continuous likelihood and derive two controlled high-dimensional limits, yielding a Hopfield-type network with continuous Hilbert-space patterns and a data-augmented Gram likelihood. The resulting algorithms are compact and use trainable circuit-prepared templates as measurement intermediaries between quantum data and classical optimization. Numerical simulations across several many-body systems demonstrate effective quantum-phase recognition and multicomponent feature extraction.
tldr: The paper constructs a restricted Boltzmann machine whose visible units are quantum states, using trainable quantum-circuit templates as hidden feature extractors for many-body phase recognition.
motivation: It aims to generalize classical RBMs to quantum-state inputs, addressing the normalization and scaling issues that arise when quantum states are treated as continuous high-dimensional visible objects.
method: Each hidden unit is prepared by a parametrized quantum circuit and converts its overlap with the input quantum state into a feature; the continuous likelihood is regularized, and two controlled high-dimensional limits are derived.
result: The limits yield a Hopfield-type network with continuous Hilbert-space patterns and a data-augmented Gram likelihood, and numerical simulations show effective quantum-phase recognition and multicomponent feature extraction across several many-body systems.
conclusion: The compact algorithms use trainable circuit-prepared templates as measurement intermediaries between quantum data and classical optimization, but the contribution is primarily a quantum machine learning application without a clear information-theoretic advance.

title: Normalizing Flow-Based Bayesian Parameter Estimation For Noisy Quantum States
authors: Hsien-Yi Hsieh, Yuan-Ting Liu, Juan Camilo Rodr{\i}guez, Yang-Yi Lee, Po-Hang Wang, Ole Steuernagel, Chien-Ming Wu, Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To extract complete information about experimental noisy quantum states, as well as correlations among different physical parameters, we develop an efficient machine learning-assisted framework with the normalizing flow based Bayesian parameter estimation (BPE). By embedding a physically interpretable parameter vector, [MATH], into the quantum state ansatzes, [MATH], the corresponding parameter distribution [MATH] is induced from BPE, based on the available experimental data [MATH]. The BPE allows us to perform parameter correlation analyses, providing powerful insights about how experimental parameters and related noise sources affect quantum features of the system. As an example, the flexibility of our framework is demonstrated using two different physical ansatzes on the optical cat state experiments, where a noisy single-photon state is added to impure squeezed state. With correlations among the Wigner function negativity, photon-addition fraction, noisy fraction, and pump powers, our framework gives interpretations for complicated experimental mechanisms in generating noisy non-Gaussian states. By leveraging normalizing flow-based neural networks and Bayesian uncertainty estimation, along with physical and experimental constraints incorporated naturally, the valuable information inferred in the posterior learning provides guidelines for experimentalists, as well as theorists, in identifying promising parameters to enhance desirable features.
tldr: Develops a normalizing flow-based Bayesian parameter estimation framework to infer parameters and correlations in noisy quantum states, demonstrated on optical cat state experiments.
motivation: To extract complete information about experimental noisy quantum states and correlations among physical parameters, providing insights into how noise sources affect quantum features.
method: Embeds a physically interpretable parameter vector into quantum state ansatzes and uses normalizing flow neural networks for Bayesian posterior estimation from experimental data, enabling parameter correlation analysis.
result: Applied to optical cat state experiments with a noisy single-photon state added to an impure squeezed state, yielding correlations among Wigner function negativity, photon-addition fraction, noisy fraction, and pump powers.
conclusion: The framework provides guidelines for experimentalists and theorists to identify promising parameters for enhancing desirable quantum features.

title: Automatic Optical Alignment Using Projective Geometry
authors: Bowen Li, Lukas Palm, Xin Wei, Marius J\"urgensen, Zeyang Li, Yiming Cady Feng, Abhishek V. Karve, Jon Simon
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning and maintaining complex optical beam paths is a central challenge across experimental science, because it is a high-dimensional task with strong cross-coupling between controls, often in systems with limited physical access. We present an automated hardware-software framework that resolves this alignment challenge using low-cost, retro-fittable motorized mounts driven by projective-geometry models and a photodiode-fed optimizer. A compact forward model describes the beam path to paraxial order with only the physical mirror angles left free, so it can be rapidly ([MATH]ms) numerically inverted to return the required mirror angles for a desired beam trajectory. A photodiode-fed optimizer then fine-tunes this geometric starting point, and converged mirror settings are tabulated for retrieval in milliseconds and actuation in seconds. We experimentally demonstrate the performance of this approach on a retro-reflected lattice atom-transport system, yielding improvements in both speed and precision over manual alignment. This framework reduces the manual effort required to align complex beam paths, enables programmable optical control in experiments with limited physical access, and enhances the scalability of complex optical architectures.
tldr: The paper presents an automated hardware-software framework that uses projective-geometry models and a photodiode-fed optimizer to align complex optical beam paths in a retro-reflected lattice atom-transport system.
motivation: Aligning and maintaining complex optical beam paths in experimental setups is a high-dimensional, strongly cross-coupled task that is labor-intensive and difficult in systems with limited physical access.
method: A compact paraxial forward model with mirror angles as the only free parameters is numerically inverted in milliseconds to give geometric starting points, which are then refined by a photodiode-fed optimizer and tabulated for fast retrieval and actuation.
result: Experimental demonstration on a retro-reflected lattice atom-transport system showed improvements in both alignment speed and precision compared with manual alignment.
conclusion: The framework reduces manual alignment effort, enables programmable optical control in hard-to-access experiments, and improves the scalability of complex optical architectures.

title: Lazy Training Of Quantum Physics Informed Neural Networks
authors: Giacomo de Palma Anderson Melchor Hernandez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the gradient-flow training dynamics of quantum physics-informed neural networks (QPINNs) for the solution of second-order elliptic partial differential equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We consider parameterized quantum circuits as function approximators and analyze their overparameterized regime through the lens of the neural tangent kernel (NTK). Our contribution is a nonasymptotic lazy-training theory for QPINNs and their variational formulation: we prove that, for sufficiently large circuit width, the nonlinear gradient flow is quantitatively approximated by a linearized NTK model, with explicit bounds depending on the number of qubits, circuit depth, circuit light-cone geometry, and the dimension of the domain of the solution to the PDE.
tldr: The paper develops a nonasymptotic lazy-training theory for quantum physics-informed neural networks (QPINNs), showing that for sufficiently wide parameterized quantum circuits the gradient-flow training dynamics are quantitatively captured by a linearized neural tangent kernel (NTK) model.
motivation: QPINNs are promising for solving PDEs, but their training dynamics are poorly understood; the authors aim to characterize when overparameterized quantum circuits behave like linear models, providing theoretical guarantees for gradient-flow optimization.
method: They analyze parameterized quantum circuits as function approximators for second-order elliptic PDEs with Dirichlet boundary conditions, using the neural tangent kernel framework to bound the deviation between the nonlinear gradient flow and its linearized NTK counterpart.
result: They prove explicit nonasymptotic bounds on the approximation of the nonlinear gradient flow by the linear NTK model, with the bounds depending on qubit number, circuit depth, circuit light-cone geometry, and the PDE domain dimension.
conclusion: The work extends lazy-training/NTK theory to the quantum PINN setting, clarifying the regimes in which QPINN training is effectively linear, though it remains a machine-learning-oriented contribution without a direct information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Binary Deletion Channel Capacity To Within One Hundredth Of A Bit
authors: Dimitris Papailiopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exact capacity of the binary deletion channel remains unknown despite decades of work on achievable rates and converse bounds. We establish a computer-assisted approximation whose error is below [MATH] bits per transmitted bit, uniformly over all deletion probabilities. The mean certified error bound, with uniform weighting of deletion probability, is below [MATH]. The estimate is the midpoint of explicit lower and upper bounds. For the converse, a stationary-source reduction is combined with finite inequalities covering every allowed input configuration. Two constructions control the unobserved input beyond a finite window: one uses a common outside survivor sequence and bounds omitted deletion patterns, while the other cancels an entropy term to make outside probabilities enter linearly. For the lower bound, finite-state inputs combine output-entropy estimates with selected disjoint counts of compatible deletion masks; independent-run inputs retain additional uncertainty about output-run boundaries. Directed numerical checks establish the finite inequalities. An analytic comparison between deletion probabilities then extends the pointwise bounds over the entire parameter range. The lower endpoint supplies rates within [MATH] bits of capacity in the asymptotic coding sense. We give the derivations, recorded computational costs, and complete numerical inputs and programs needed to verify the result.
tldr: A computer-assisted determination of the binary deletion channel capacity to within roughly one hundredth of a bit, uniformly over all deletion probabilities.
motivation: The exact capacity of the binary deletion channel has remained unknown for decades, with only loose achievable rates and converse bounds available; this work aims to pin it down numerically to high precision.
method: Explicit lower and upper bounds are constructed: the converse uses a stationary-source reduction plus finite inequalities controlling unobserved input beyond a finite window, while the lower bound uses finite-state and independent-run input distributions with output-entropy and disjoint deletion-mask counting arguments; directed numerical and analytic checks certify the finite inequalities and extend them uniformly.
result: The midpoint of the certified bounds yields an estimate whose error is below one hundredth of a bit per transmitted bit for all deletion probabilities, with a smaller mean certified error under uniform weighting.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorously verifiable, computer-assisted approximation of the deletion channel capacity, along with programs and numerical inputs needed to reproduce the certificate.

title: On The Leakage Of Massey Secret Sharing Schemes Under Linear Computations
authors: Nadja Aoutouf (X, SURYCAT), Daniel Augot
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leakage attacks on secret sharing schemes exploit partial information about individual shares to recover the underlying secret. In coding theory, linear exact repair schemes (LERSs) enable the recovery of one codeword symbol from a small amount of information obtained from the remaining symbols, provided that the code has sufficiently low rate. This can be interpreted as recovering the secret from partial information, namely subfield symbols, of the shares. Recently, a randomized construction based on subfield subcodes was proposed for constructing LERS-derived leakage attacks against Massey secret sharing schemes based on general linear codes. We extend this framework to multiple shared secrets whose corresponding shares are related through linear computations, with leakage also allowed on the computation outcomes. More precisely, we consider N secrets, of which K [MATH] N are linearly independent input values and the remaining N -K secrets are determined by linear computations on these inputs. We analyse the existence of LERS-derived leakage that exploits this structure. We first study the case of addition and then generalize our construction to arbitrary linear computations. Our analysis applies to general linear codes of length n+1 and dimension k over F\_{q^m} with k [MATH] N n/(Km), and supports arbitrary linear computations, whereas the previous subfield subcode construction only applies to k [MATH] n/m -1. Consequently, exploiting the linear relations enables LERS based leakage which extend the range of code parameters vulnerable to such attacks. Finally, identical leakage functions can arise for certain linear relations, making this a more realistic yet still potentially powerful attack model. Finally, simulations indicate that identical leakage functions can be used for certain linear relations, yielding a more realistic attack model.
tldr: The paper extends LERS-derived leakage attacks on Massey secret sharing schemes to multiple shared secrets related by linear computations.
motivation: Leakage attacks on secret sharing exploit partial share information; prior work on subfield-subcode constructions only handled a single secret or restrictive code rates, so extending to linearly related secrets broadens the attack surface.
method: The authors generalize a randomized subfield-subcode construction for linear exact repair schemes to N secrets, K linearly independent inputs and N-K linearly computed outputs, first for addition and then for arbitrary linear computations over F_{q^m}.
result: The construction applies to general linear codes with k < n/(Km), extending the vulnerable parameter range beyond the previous k < n/m - 1, and shows that identical leakage functions can arise for certain linear relations.
conclusion: Exploiting linear relations among secrets enables more realistic and powerful LERS-based leakage attacks on Massey secret sharing schemes, widening the set of vulnerable code parameters.

title: Some Mds And Acd Codes Over Commutative Non-unital Rings Of Orders 4 And 9 (Revision)
authors: Jon-Lark Kim, Marvin Olavides, Young Gun Roe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There are eleven finite rings of order [MATH] denoted by [MATH] to [MATH] in alphabetical order. In particular, we consider [MATH] and [MATH] which are commutative non-unital rings of orders 4 and 9 defined by generators and relations as \[I_{p}=\left\langle a,b\mid pa=pb=0,\:a^{2}=b,\:ab=0\right\rangle\] for [MATH] respectively. Alahmadi et al. studied codes over these rings. In this paper, we study additive complementary dual (ACD) codes over the rings [MATH] and [MATH]. We show relations between ACD codes over [MATH] and binary linear complementary dual (LCD) codes using a reduction map from [MATH] to [MATH], and between ACD codes over [MATH] and ternary LCD codes using a reduction map from [MATH] to [MATH]. Using the first relation, we classify ACD codes over [MATH] with the highest minimum distances for [MATH] and partially for [MATH]. It turns out that they are maximum distance separable (MDS) codes. Using the second relation, we classify ACD codes over [MATH] with the highest minimum Lee distances for [MATH] and partially for [MATH]. We generalize the two relations into a relation between ACD codes over [MATH] and [MATH]-ary LCD codes using a reduction map from [MATH] to [MATH]. This is a correction of the paper published in Advances in Mathematics of Communications, Volume 24, pages 61-76, 2026. In particular, we corrected the statements of Theorems 3.5, 4.7, 4.8, and their proofs.
tldr: The paper studies additive complementary dual (ACD) codes over two commutative non-unital rings of orders 4 and 9, relating them to binary and ternary LCD codes and classifying MDS codes with optimal minimum distances.
motivation: Codes over finite rings extend classical coding theory, and ACD codes are the ring analogue of linear complementary dual (LCD) codes, which are useful for cryptography and error correction.
method: The authors use reduction maps from the rings to finite fields to connect ACD codes over the rings to binary and ternary LCD codes, and then classify ACD codes with the highest minimum distance (or Lee distance).
result: They establish relations between ACD codes and LCD codes, classify ACD codes with the highest minimum distances for small lengths, and show that these optimal codes are maximum distance separable (MDS).
conclusion: The relations are generalized to a connection between ACD codes over Z_{p^2} and p-ary LCD codes, and the paper corrects several theorems from a previous publication.

title: Improving Sample Efficiency In Peptide-HLA Binding Prediction With Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks
authors: Chenyan Jia, Cong Guo, Siyue Chen, Pengpeng Ye, Xiaochun Chen
