At each nontrivial successor step, the projection has two-point fibres over a chosen closed set and singleton fibres elsewhere; this changes the weak-star limit of a selected sequence of finitely supported measures. We also prove that, for compact [MATH], the existence of an infinite-dimensional separable quotient of [MATH] is equivalent to the existence of an infinite-dimensional metrisable quotient.
tldr: Under Jensen's diamond principle, the authors construct an Efimov compact space K such that C(K) has no infinite-dimensional Hausdorff separable linear quotient.
motivation: The paper studies separable quotients of Banach spaces of continuous functions and pointwise function spaces, addressing structural questions in functional analysis and set-theoretic topology.
method: They build K as an inverse limit of compact metrisable spaces indexed by countable ordinals, using successor-step projections with two-point fibres over chosen closed sets to alter weak-star limits of finitely supported measures.
result: The constructed space is separable, crowded, has weight and cardinality continuum, and is Efimov; moreover, for compact K, existence of an infinite-dimensional separable quotient of C(K) is equivalent to existence of an infinite-dimensional metrisable quotient.
conclusion: This provides a consistent example showing failure of separable quotients for pointwise function spaces, contributing to the theory of Efimov spaces and Banach-space quotients.

title: Traces Of Besov And Lizorkin--Triebel Spaces To Thick Subsets Of $\mathbb{R}^n$
authors: Aleksei Y. Chikalov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and let [MATH] be a closed [MATH]-thick set. Given [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], we provide an intrinsic description of the trace-space of the Besov space [MATH] to [MATH]. If, in addition, [MATH], we give an intrinsic description of the trace-space of the Lizorkin--Triebel space [MATH] to [MATH].
tldr: The paper gives intrinsic descriptions of trace spaces of Besov and Lizorkin–Triebel spaces on thick subsets of R^n.
motivation: Trace spaces of function spaces on non-smooth sets are important in analysis, but the specific setting of thick subsets is not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The author uses intrinsic characterizations of Besov and Lizorkin–Triebel spaces and extends them to closed d-thick sets in Euclidean space.
result: For a closed d-thick set and appropriate parameters, the trace space of the Besov space is described intrinsically, and a similar description is given for the Lizorkin–Triebel space under an additional condition.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical function space theory and has no direct relevance to the researcher's interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pdnqp: A GPU-based Factorization-free Method For Large-scale Nonconvex Quadratic Programming
authors: Haihao Lu Zixi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale nonconvex quadratic programming remains challenging because the sparse matrix factorizations used by many existing solvers can incur substantial computational and memory costs and are difficult to parallelize efficiently on GPUs. We present PDNQP, a factorization-free first-order solver for finding stationary points of large-scale nonconvex quadratic programs. The method combines a proximal augmented-Lagrangian framework with restarted accelerated primal--dual hybrid gradient to solve the resulting strongly convex QP subproblems. Its key ingredients are a residual-form reformulation that avoids penalty-dependent normal matrices and preserves a fixed sparse constraint operator across outer iterations, and an adaptive strategy that coordinates inner-solve accuracy with outer progress. The resulting computations rely on sparse matrix--vector products, projections, and vector operations suited to GPU execution. On [MATH] nonconvex CUTEst instances, PDNQP achieves the highest success rate among the tested solvers at both accuracy levels. With absolute and relative tolerances set to [MATH], it achieves speedups of [MATH]--[MATH] in shifted geometric mean runtime; at [MATH], its aggregate runtime remains comparable to that of the fastest tested solvers. On [MATH] large-scale synthetic nonconvex QPs with approximately one million variables each, PDNQP returns points satisfying the common external termination criteria on [MATH] instances, while none of the other tested solvers succeeds under the same experimental protocol.
tldr: PDNQP is a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for finding stationary points of large-scale nonconvex quadratic programs.
motivation: Existing sparse matrix factorization-based solvers for large-scale nonconvex QPs incur heavy computational and memory costs and parallelize poorly on GPUs.
method: The solver couples a proximal augmented-Lagrangian framework with restarted accelerated primal-dual hybrid gradient, using a residual-form reformulation with a fixed sparse constraint operator and an adaptive inner-solve accuracy strategy, relying only on sparse matrix-vector products, projections, and vector operations suited to GPU execution.
result: On nonconvex CUTEst instances it attains the highest success rate among tested solvers with speedups of up to orders of magnitude in shifted geometric mean runtime, and on million-variable synthetic QPs it satisfies external termination criteria where all other tested solvers fail.
conclusion: GPU-friendly, factorization-free first-order methods can scale nonconvex quadratic programming to problem sizes beyond the reach of conventional factorization-based solvers.

title: The Exact Region Determined By Spearman's Rho And Gini's Gamma
authors: Jonathan Ansari, Marcus Rockel, Stefanie Steinma\ss{}l
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the exact attainable region of Spearman's rho and Gini's gamma over all bivariate copulas, resolving the remaining pairwise exact-region problem among Spearman's rho, Kendall's tau, Gini's gamma, Blomqvist's beta and Spearman's footrule. We give an explicit parametrization of the rho-maximal boundary for prescribed Gini's gamma and construct copulas attaining every boundary point. The boundary consists of an elementary arc up to a single junction and, beyond it, countably many algebraic pieces accumulating at comonotonicity. This description also gives the largest possible value of [MATH] and the sharp thresholds beyond which rho and gamma must have the same sign. Our proof separates the signs and magnitudes of centred ranks, reducing the optimization of linear combinations of [MATH] and [MATH] to an optimal transport problem for two uniform magnitudes. The extremizers combine a central antidiagonal block with rescaled auxiliary transport optimizers, and global optimality follows from a Kantorovich dual potential obtained by gluing the corresponding dual pieces.
tldr: The paper determines the exact attainable region of Spearman's rho and Gini's gamma over all bivariate copulas, resolving the remaining pairwise exact-region problem among several rank dependence measures.
motivation: The exact pairwise dependence regions among common rank correlation measures were not fully known, and this work aims to complete that classification.
method: The proof separates signs and magnitudes of centered ranks, reducing the optimization of linear combinations to an optimal transport problem for two uniform magnitudes, with extremizers built from a central antidiagonal block and rescaled auxiliary optimizers.
result: It gives an explicit parametrization of the rho-maximal boundary for prescribed Gini's gamma, shows the boundary consists of an elementary arc, a junction, and countably many algebraic pieces accumulating at comonotonicity, and derives sharp sign thresholds.
conclusion: The exact rho-gamma region is completely characterized, yielding the largest possible value of the relevant linear combination and thresholds beyond which rho and gamma must share a sign.

title: Validating Hexahedra Through Their Boundaries
authors: Paul Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trilinear hexahedral mesh elements are used in finite element analysis to simulate volumetric phenomena. Realism of the simulation mandates that mesh elements through the trilinear map maintain positive volume, or mathematically, that the trilinear map maintains positive Jacobian determinant (jacdet). While jacdet positivity generally needs to be verified in the full element volume, we prove Knupp's conjecture which posits that for trilinear hexahedra, jacdet positivity on the boundary of the element is sufficient to guarantee positivity in the entire element. We further prove that for any valid hexahedron, its globally minimal jacdet must reside on the boundary. Lastly, we prove that the globally minimal jacdet on the boundary of a hexahedron, valid or not, must be achieved within a finite set of candidate points that can be determined by quartic root finding. Combining these results, we can algorithmically validate a hexahedron through evaluation of its jacdet on a finite set of boundary points.
tldr: The paper proves Knupp's conjecture that Jacobian determinant positivity on the boundary of a trilinear hexahedron guarantees positivity throughout the element, enabling algorithmic validation via finite boundary evaluations.
motivation: Finite element simulations require hexahedral mesh elements to maintain positive Jacobian determinant for realism, but verifying positivity over the entire element volume is computationally expensive.
method: The authors prove that the globally minimal Jacobian determinant of a valid hexahedron lies on its boundary, and that this boundary minimum can be found within a finite set of candidate points using quartic root finding.
result: It is shown that boundary positivity implies interior positivity, and an algorithm is provided that validates a hexahedron by evaluating the Jacobian determinant at a finite set of boundary points.
conclusion: This work resolves a long-standing conjecture and offers a practical method for hexahedral mesh validation, though it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Sharp Variational, Jump And Oscillation Bounds In A General Gaussian Context
authors: Valentina Casarino, Paolo Ciatti, Peter Sj\"ogren
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a general, nonsymmetric Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup [MATH]. We prove an [MATH] bound for the jump quasi-seminorms for [MATH] and a weak type (1,1) oscillation inequality, both with respect to the invariant measure. These results are established for the order [MATH]. To do so, we analyze specific components of [MATH], by distinguishing between small and large values of [MATH], and between local and global spatial zones. This decomposition allows us to explicitly identify which parts of the semigroup remain bounded and which are responsible for the failure of boundedness, both in a weak and in a strong sense, even with respect to Lebesgue measure.
tldr: The paper proves sharp variational, jump, and weak-type oscillation bounds for a general nonsymmetric Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup in a harmonic analysis setting.
motivation: The authors aim to establish boundedness properties for components of a nonsymmetric Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup and identify which parts fail boundedness with respect to invariant and Lebesgue measures.
method: They decompose the semigroup into small/large parameter and local/global spatial zones to analyze jump quasi-seminorms and oscillation inequalities.
result: They obtain an L^p bound for jump quasi-seminorms and a weak type (1,1) oscillation inequality for order p, explicitly separating bounded and unbounded parts.
conclusion: The work provides sharp bounds in a general Gaussian context, clarifying the boundedness structure of nonsymmetric Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroups.

title: Stability And Logarithmic Foliations On Complex Projective Spaces
authors: Bruno Sc\'ardua V\'ictor Le\'on
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Lyapunov-type stability for invariant algebraic divisors of codimension-one holomorphic foliations on complex projective spaces. Motivated by the notion of [MATH]-stability introduced in for plane singularities, we define a projective stability condition which is compatible with the logarithmic setting and controls leafwise holonomy along the regular part of the invariant divisor, while discarding any stability requirement inside prescribed neighborhoods of its singular locus. Our main result then is a global projective counterpart of the local classification in : for a maximal invariant algebraic divisor, projective [MATH]-stability together with non-dicritical non-nodal generalized-curve singularities on a generic plane section forces the ambient foliation to be globally logarithmic. As an application we obtain a topological rigidity consequence on [MATH] for logarithmic foliations under mild generic conditions. The proof of the main theorem is based on propagating the consequences of the stability hypothesis through the reduction tree by means of an explicit Dulac transport argument, together with the classification of [MATH]-stable groups of germs of one-dimensional complex diffeomorphisms.
tldr: The paper studies Lyapunov-type stability for invariant algebraic divisors of codimension-one holomorphic foliations on complex projective spaces and proves a global logarithmic foliation theorem under projective stability conditions.
motivation: The work is motivated by extending the notion of M-stability from plane singularities to a projective setting compatible with logarithmic foliations, aiming to understand when an ambient foliation must be globally logarithmic.
method: The authors introduce a projective stability condition controlling leafwise holonomy along the regular part of an invariant divisor while ignoring prescribed neighborhoods of singularities, and use a Dulac transport argument through the reduction tree together with the classification of M-stable groups of germs of one-dimensional complex diffeomorphisms.
result: For a maximal invariant algebraic divisor, projective M-stability plus non-dicritical non-nodal generalized-curve singularities on a generic plane section forces the ambient foliation to be globally logarithmic; an application yields topological rigidity for logarithmic foliations under mild generic conditions.
conclusion: The paper establishes a global projective counterpart to local classification results and derives rigidity consequences for logarithmic foliations, contributing to the theory of holomorphic foliations and complex projective geometry.

title: FloatLib: Verified Floating-Point Arithmetic In Lean
authors: Robert Joseph George, Will Adkisson, Anima Anandkumar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present FloatLib, a verified arbitrary-precision floating-point arithmetic library in Lean 4 that combines broad format coverage, machine-checked correctness, and efficient certified execution. To our knowledge, FloatLib is the first Lean library to unify IEEE binary and decimal arithmetic, arbitrary-width posits, P3109, and user-defined formats and rounding rules behind interchangeable certified software backends. Every certified backend is proved equal to a complete encoded specification, preserving signed zeros and exceptional values, while numerical theorems connect execution to real rounding, error bounds, and exactness. FloatLib combines exhaustive certified tables for small formats with verified word and limb kernels based on guard-and-sticky invariants and independently checked quotient candidates. Its posit development additionally proves standard rounding thresholds and exact quire accumulation within capacity for arbitrary widths. Across matched workloads, FloatLib achieves speedups of up to 1.46x over FLoPS and 116x over Universal, while remaining slower in some regimes such as binary arithmetic against MPFR. Independent conformance testing includes more than 102 million TestFloat evaluations with zero differences under the tested relation. We release the library, proofs, benchmarks, evaluation data, and guide as open source.
tldr: FloatLib is a verified arbitrary-precision floating-point arithmetic library in Lean 4 that unifies IEEE binary/decimal, posits, P3109, and user-defined formats with certified backends.
motivation: Floating-point arithmetic is error-prone and existing verified libraries have limited format coverage or performance; FloatLib aims to provide broad, machine-checked correctness with efficient certified execution.
method: The library combines exhaustive certified tables for small formats with verified word and limb kernels based on guard-and-sticky invariants and independently checked quotient candidates, covering IEEE binary/decimal, arbitrary-width posits, P3109, and user-defined formats.
result: FloatLib achieves speedups up to 1.46x over FLoPS and 116x over Universal in matched workloads, passes more than 102 million TestFloat evaluations with zero differences under the tested relation, and proves standard rounding thresholds and exact quire accumulation for posits.
conclusion: FloatLib provides a unified, verified floating-point framework with strong conformance and performance, released as open source, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Periodic And Aperiodic Optimal Strategies In Solvency Games
authors: Quentin Guilmant, Florian Luca, Richard Mayr, Jo\"el Ouaknine, James Worrell
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solvency games are a gambling problem on infinite-state Markov decision processes in which the state [MATH] represents an investor's fortune. In every round, the investor chooses an action from a finite action set, and every action yields a distribution over integer-valued gains in an interval [MATH]. The risk-averse investor wants to minimise the probability of eventual ruin (reaching a fortune [MATH]). It was shown in [Berger et al.] that memoryless deterministic optimal strategies exist, but they are not eventually constant in general. Even in the special case of gains in [MATH], the optimal strategy may need to make use of two different actions at arbitrarily high fortunes. We show that optimal strategies in solvency games need not be ultimately periodic in general (thus disproving a 2012 conjecture of Kuera). Already in the case of gains in [MATH], it is possible for the optimal strategy to be unique but aperiodic. For gains in [MATH], there always exists an ultimately periodic optimal strategy whose tail is constant or alternates between two actions. Finally, we show that the optimal strategy is computable if it is unique. Moreover, (some) optimal strategy can always be computed in the case of gains in [MATH] for any [MATH]. Computability in the general case however remains open.
tldr: The paper studies optimal strategies in solvency games, showing that optimal strategies need not be ultimately periodic and investigating their computability.
motivation: Solvency games model risk-averse investment on infinite-state Markov decision processes, and a 2012 conjecture claimed optimal strategies are ultimately periodic; this work resolves that conjecture.
method: The authors analyze optimal strategies for minimizing ruin probability in solvency games with integer-valued gains, constructing counterexamples and proving structural results for special gain sets.
result: They disprove the ultimate periodicity conjecture, show unique optimal strategies can be aperiodic even for small gain sets, prove existence of ultimately periodic optima for certain restricted gains, and establish computability when the optimal strategy is unique.
conclusion: Optimal strategies in solvency games are more complex than previously conjectured; computability in the general case remains open.

title: Concurrency, Causality And Conflict Via Independence In Reversible Calculi
authors: Cl\'ement Aubert (augusta University), Gabriele Cecilia (augusta University), Iain C. C. Phillips (imperial College London), Irek Ulidowski
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Among the different ways of approaching the semantics of process calculi, true-concurrency models stand out for their ability to highlight subtle interplays between events. At their heart lie three crucial relations: concurrency, causality and conflict. This paper shows that reversibility, when endowed with a notion of independence, provides a rich tooling to study and characterise these true-concurrency relations. First, we prove that systems admitting pre-reversibility (i.e., that can be extended with an independence relation satisfying some basic axioms) have a unique notion of independence, events, concurrency, causality and conflict. We then analyse the relationship between independence and the true-concurrency relations, establishing novel independence-based characterisations of causality and conflict. Our second series of contributions revolves around two concrete process calculi and two syntactic notions defined on their transition labels, namely independence and dependence; we prove that they partition connected transitions and characterise elegantly concurrency on adjacent transitions. This part of our development was machine-checked using the proof assistant Beluga. Last, we study how the key mechanism commonly used in reversible process algebra can be used as a proxy to retrieve causality and core independence on past events. We conclude by discussing how our results extend beyond reversible systems.
tldr: This paper uses reversibility and independence relations to characterize true-concurrency relations—concurrency, causality, and conflict—in reversible process calculi.
motivation: The authors aim to provide richer semantic tools for studying true concurrency by leveraging reversibility and independence, allowing unique characterizations of concurrency, causality, and conflict in process calculi.
method: They define pre-reversibility and independence axioms, prove uniqueness of independence and associated relations, analyze independence-based characterizations of causality and conflict, and formalize results for two calculi using the Beluga proof assistant.
result: They establish novel independence-based characterizations of causality and conflict, show that syntactic independence and dependence partition connected transitions and characterize concurrency, and demonstrate how reversible mechanisms recover past causality and core independence.
conclusion: The work shows that reversibility with independence provides a powerful framework for true-concurrency semantics, with potential extensions beyond reversible systems.

title: Condorcet-type Properties Of The Linear Ordering Problem With Ties
authors: Noriyoshi Sukegawa Daichi Kawashima
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kemeny rule aggregates multiple strict rankings into a single strict ranking that minimizes the sum of its distances from the input rankings. The resulting optimization problem, called the Kemeny problem (), is a special case of the linear ordering problem (). The Kemeny rule satisfies several desirable properties in social choice theory, including the extended Condorcet criterion (). Ando et al. strengthened this result by introducing the strong Condorcet criterion () and showing that it holds for every optimal solution to an arbitrary instance. Yoo and Escobedo extended the Kemeny rule to rankings with ties and showed that the resulting rule satisfies the non-strict extended Condorcet criterion (). This criterion gives a condition under which one candidate must be ranked strictly above another in every optimal solution. In this paper, we introduce the non-strict strong Condorcet criterion (), a counterpart of the for rankings with ties, and show that it holds for every optimal solution to an arbitrary instance of the linear ordering problem with ties (). We also establish a complementary structural property that gives conditions under which two candidates must be tied in every optimal solution to an arbitrary instance.
tldr: This paper introduces non-strict strong Condorcet criteria for the linear ordering problem with ties, extending social-choice aggregation results for the Kemeny rule.
motivation: The Kemeny rule and its Condorcet-type properties are central to social choice theory, and prior work extended the Kemeny rule to rankings with ties but only established the non-strict extended Condorcet criterion.
method: The authors define a non-strict strong Condorcet criterion for rankings with ties and prove that it holds for every optimal solution of the linear ordering problem with ties, along with a complementary structural tie condition.
result: The new criterion is shown to hold universally for all optimal solutions to arbitrary instances, and a complementary property gives conditions under which two candidates must be tied in every optimal solution.
conclusion: The results strengthen the theoretical understanding of the linear ordering problem with ties and extend Condorcet-type guarantees to non-strict rankings.

title: A Separation Between Distribution-Free Sq Learning And Dimension Complexity
authors: Shyamal Patel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exists a class of boolean functions C such that [MATH] there is a distribution-independent statistical query algorithm for learning C that makes a polynomial number of queries of inverse polynomial tolerance and [MATH] for any set of functions [MATH] such that for all [MATH] C we can write [MATH] for some set of weights [MATH], we must have that [MATH]. This gives a superpolynomial separation between dimension complexity and the query complexity of distribution-free learning in the statistical query model, negatively answering a question of Feldman, Kamath, and Srebro [FKS26]. Our construction C is a subclass of DNFs, and the proof is a simple consequence of recent progress on agnostically learning conjunctions [DKR25,CPS26] and the work of Razborov and Sherstov on the sign rank of DNFs [RS10].
tldr: The paper shows a superpolynomial separation between dimension complexity and distribution-free statistical query learning, negatively answering a question of Feldman, Kamath, and Srebro.
motivation: To separate dimension complexity from the query complexity of distribution-free learning in the statistical query model, addressing an open problem.
method: Constructs a subclass of DNFs and leverages recent progress on agnostically learning conjunctions and the Razborov-Sherstov bound on the sign rank of DNFs.
result: There exists a class of boolean functions learnable by a distribution-independent SQ algorithm with polynomial queries and inverse polynomial tolerance, yet having superpolynomial dimension complexity.
conclusion: Dimension complexity does not characterize distribution-free SQ learning, resolving the open question negatively.

title: Sybil-TraceGuard: Traceability-enhanced Sybil Guardian For Connected And Autonomous Vehicles Using Dynamic Semi-supervised Gnn
authors: Qian Xu, Jiaxun Zhang, Chengyue Wang, Zhenning Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) face severe Sybil attacks, where attackers exploit privacy-preserving pseudonym-switching mechanisms to anomaly alternate identities while forging Basic Safety Messages (BSMs). Although existing schemes can flag suspicious behaviors, these temporally fragmented Sybil identities render traditional single-point and sequence-based deep learning methods ineffective. Linking these fragmented identities back to the source attacker is essential for root-cause elimination, particularly under extreme label scarcity. Therefore, the Sybil-TraceGuard is proposed as a dynamic semi-supervised spatio-temporal GNN framework for Sybil Guardian, prioritizing "who is responsible" over "whether an attack is happening". It comprises four tightly coupled modules: Incremental Stream Attack Detection (ISAD) for efficient Sybil attack pre-screening; the Dynamic Topology-aware Constructor (DTC) for constructing spatio-temporal dynamic graphs; the Spatial GAT-Encoder with Multi-head Attention (SGEM) to capture multi-identity logical conflicts in spatial interactions; and the Multi-scale Spatio-Temporal Audit (MSTA) to audit short-term and long-term temporal inconsistencies. These modules are optimized within a semi-supervised Mean-Teacher framework via feature-edge shuffling perturbations, regularizing the latent feature space using minimal labels. Experiments across four Sybil attack scenarios demonstrate that Sybil-TraceGuard effectively links fragmented pseudonyms to source attackers. It outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across unlabeled ratios of 0.70-0.95, maintaining high stability and sensitivity despite extreme class imbalance and varying hyperparameter settings.
tldr: Sybil-TraceGuard is a dynamic semi-supervised spatio-temporal GNN framework for detecting and tracing Sybil attacks in connected and autonomous vehicles under extreme label scarcity.
motivation: CAVs are vulnerable to Sybil attacks where attackers switch pseudonyms to forge safety messages, and existing detection methods fail to link fragmented identities back to the source attacker, especially with few labels.
method: The framework combines incremental stream attack detection, dynamic topology-aware graph construction, a spatial GAT encoder with multi-head attention, and multi-scale spatio-temporal auditing, optimized in a semi-supervised Mean-Teacher setup with feature-edge shuffling perturbations.
result: Across four Sybil attack scenarios, Sybil-TraceGuard effectively links fragmented pseudonyms to source attackers and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines at unlabeled ratios of 0.70–0.95, maintaining stability under class imbalance.
conclusion: The proposed traceability-enhanced Sybil guardian prioritizes identifying responsible attackers over merely detecting attacks and shows strong performance in low-label CAV security settings.

title: Mind The Gap: How Sbom Specification Ambiguities Lead To Divergent Software Bills Of Materials. An Empirical Tool Study
authors: Alan Prado (diverse), Olivier Zendra (diverse), Philippe Boinot (ANSSI), Olivier Barais
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) will become mandatory starting in December 2027 under the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) [8]. Although previous studies have highlighted significant differences among SBOM generators, the reasons for these discrepancies remain unknown, as does whether they stem from implementation errors or deliberate design choices. In this paper, we evaluate three widely used SBOM generators across more than 3,000 JavaScript and Rust projects, using a groundtruth baseline derived from dependency lockfiles. Our results show that these tools diverge in terms of both dependency coverage and SBOM completeness. Importantly, most of these discrepancies are systematic rather than accidental: they arise from differing assumptions regarding dependency scope, naming, provenance, and representation, while others reflect inconsistent support for fields defined in SBOM specifications. These findings demonstrate that many of the observed discrepancies cannot simply be ''fixed'': they require clearer standardization. As SBOM generation becomes a legal compliance requirement, the choice of tool itself can influence the resulting SBOM, potentially becoming a source of undetected non-compliance. We argue that future SBOM standards should define canonical rules regarding dependency scope, provenance, and representation to improve interoperability and compliance.
tldr: An empirical study of three SBOM generators across 3,000+ JavaScript and Rust projects reveals systematic discrepancies due to specification ambiguities and inconsistent field support.
motivation: SBOMs will become mandatory under the European Cyber Resilience Act, but differences among generators are poorly understood, risking undetected non-compliance.
method: The authors compare three widely used SBOM generators against a ground-truth baseline from dependency lockfiles for over 3,000 projects in JavaScript and Rust.
result: Tools diverge in dependency coverage and SBOM completeness, with most discrepancies being systematic and rooted in differing assumptions about scope, naming, provenance, and representation rather than accidental implementation errors.
conclusion: Future SBOM standards must define canonical rules to improve interoperability and compliance, as tool choice alone can influence SBOM content and legal compliance.

title: Competition, Collusion, And Corruption: The Spectrum Of Mev Attacks On DAG-Based Bft Consensus Protocols
authors: Iliya Mirzaei, Heer Patel, Chenyuan Wu, Mohammad Javad Amiri
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Byzantine Fault-Tolerant (BFT) protocols guarantee safety and liveness despite the malicious failure of nodes. However, they do not prevent adversarial manipulation of transaction order, where the order a proposer assigns diverges from the order in which clients submitted their transactions. Exploiting this discretion for profit is known as maximal extractable value (MEV), and it is intensified in DAG-based BFT protocols, where every replica proposes blocks concurrently rather than routing transactions through a single designated proposer each round. The proliferation of MEV attacks on DAG-based BFT protocols has made the resulting landscape difficult to navigate: attacks are reported individually, on different protocols, and under different metrics, making it unclear whether two attacks differ fundamentally or merely in how they are described. This paper closes that gap by presenting an attack space for MEV on DAG-based BFT protocols, organized around four families: the adversary, the protocol, the target, and the deployment. For each family, we identify the dimensions that shape an attack's impact. Each point in the attack space fixes one value per dimension, thereby representing a distinct, potential MEV attack, which can then be instantiated on a specific DAG-based BFT protocol. We perform a set of experiments, each isolating a single dimension where the protocol permits it, to empirically measure its effect on the success rate of MEV attacks against six production DAG-based BFT protocols. Our experimental evaluation reveals that every protocol we evaluate is vulnerable to at least a subset of the MEV attacks in this space, and that which attacks succeed is mostly dictated by the protocol's own design rather than by attacker effort.
tldr: This paper presents an attack space for maximal extractable value (MEV) on DAG-based Byzantine Fault-Tolerant consensus protocols and empirically evaluates six production protocols.
motivation: MEV attacks on DAG-based BFT protocols are reported inconsistently, making it hard to compare attacks across protocols and metrics.
method: The authors organize MEV attacks along four families—adversary, protocol, target, and deployment—and run experiments isolating dimensions to measure attack success rates against six production DAG-based BFT protocols.
result: Every evaluated protocol is vulnerable to some subset of MEV attacks, and attack success is mostly determined by protocol design rather than attacker effort.
conclusion: The proposed attack space helps systematize MEV vulnerabilities in DAG-based BFT consensus and highlights the need for protocol-level mitigations.

title: Dense Pinwheel Packing Is Strongly NP-Complete
authors: Yusuke Kobayashi, Bingkai Lin, Joseph Swernofsky
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An instance of {\sc Pinwheel Packing} is a list of positive integers [MATH]. A feasible schedule assigns one task to every integer time so that every interval of [MATH] consecutive times contains task [MATH]. The instance is when [MATH]. We prove that {\sc Dense Pinwheel Packing} is NP-complete even when every period is encoded in unary and equal periods are listed as distinct tasks. Consequently, the usual binary-encoded problem is strongly NP-complete. Kleinberg and Mishra also prove NP-completeness \cite[Corollary~5.1]{KleinbergMishra2026}, but their reduction uses periods of exponential numerical size and therefore yields only weak NP-hardness. Our proof uses a direct reduction from triangle partition in a sparse tripartite graph. If each of the three parts of the source graph has [MATH] vertices, the reduction produces [MATH] explicitly listed tasks, each with period [MATH]; consequently, its full unary encoding has length [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that Dense Pinwheel Packing is NP-complete under unary encoding and strongly NP-complete under binary encoding.
motivation: Pinwheel Packing is a scheduling problem where prior NP-completeness proof used periods of exponential size, yielding only weak NP-hardness; the authors aim to establish strong NP-completeness.
method: The proof uses a direct reduction from triangle partition in a sparse tripartite graph, producing an instance with explicitly listed tasks and periods polynomial in the source graph size.
result: Dense Pinwheel Packing remains NP-complete even when every period is encoded in unary and equal periods are listed as distinct tasks, implying the usual binary-encoded problem is strongly NP-complete.
conclusion: The work resolves the complexity status of Dense Pinwheel Packing by establishing strong NP-completeness, strengthening previous weak NP-hardness results.

title: Tri-Hybrid Beamforming Design For Large-Scale Mimo Isac Systems
authors: Tianyu Fang, Mengyuan Ma, Markku Juntti, Inkyu Lee, Joonhyuk Kang, Nhan Thanh Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tri-hybrid multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures have been proposed as a promising solution for enabling energy-efficient communications systems in large-scale antenna arrays by replacing conventional antenna arrays in hybrid beamforming (HBF) systems with low-cost dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs). In this work, we investigate beamforming design for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems based on tri-HBF architectures, with the objective of jointly enhancing the communications sum rate and sensing sum mutual information. Specifically, we formulate a weighted multi-objective optimization problem that balances communications throughput and sensing mutual information, subject to a total transmit power consumption constraint and the physical limitations inherent to tri-HBF architectures. By exploiting the problem structure, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm with closed-form updates to solve the non-convex optimization problem with low complexity. Numerical results are provided to evaluate the performance of the proposed tri-HBF architecture in various setups. The results demonstrate that the proposed tri-HBF architecture can achieve significant improvement in energy efficiency (EE) compared to the conventional hybrid MIMO and DMA-only configurations, at the cost of minor degradations in sum rate and sensing mutual information.
tldr: This paper designs a tri-hybrid beamforming architecture using dynamic metasurface antennas for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in large-scale MIMO systems, jointly optimizing communications sum rate and sensing mutual information.
motivation: Conventional hybrid beamforming with large antenna arrays is energy-inefficient; replacing parts of the array with low-cost dynamic metasurface antennas promises better energy efficiency for ISAC systems.
method: The authors formulate a weighted multi-objective non-convex optimization problem balancing communications throughput and sensing mutual information under transmit power and tri-HBF hardware constraints, and solve it with a low-complexity iterative algorithm using closed-form updates.
result: Numerical simulations show the proposed tri-hybrid architecture achieves significant energy-efficiency gains over conventional hybrid MIMO and DMA-only configurations, with only minor degradation in sum rate and sensing mutual information.
conclusion: Tri-hybrid beamforming offers an attractive energy-efficient design for large-scale MIMO ISAC systems, though the work remains a classical wireless communications engineering contribution.

title: A Scalable Trust Discovery Architecture For The Internet Of Agents
authors: Song Zhang, Jiankang Yao, Hongtao Li, Xiaojun Zhang, Xugang Shen, Xin Li, Yanbiao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Internet of Agents is expected to enable large numbers of autonomous agents to discover, verify, and collaborate with each other across heterogeneous platforms. However, current agent protocols mainly address tool invocation and inter-agent communication, leaving scalable agent registration, trustworthy identification, and capability-oriented discovery largely unresolved. To address this, this paper proposes a scalable trust discovery architecture for the Internet of Agents. The proposed architecture adopts a hierarchical and distributed design consisting of three layers: Agent Root for trusted registry governance, Agent Registry for agent registration and metadata publication, and Agent Resolver for distributed capability discovery and trust-aware resolution. The architecture further introduces a registry-suffix-anchored composite identity scheme, which binds an agent native identifier to a trusted registry suffix to generate a globally discoverable identity. It also incorporates a dual-certificate and multi-level authentication mechanism to strengthen identity trust among agents. We implement a prototype and evaluate it through large-scale agent registration and resolution experiments. The prototype achieves an average registration latency of 58ms and an average discovery latency of 25ms, and it supports more than 19,000 registration requests per second and more than 29,000 agent discovery requests per second. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed architecture, providing a practical approach toward scalable and identity-trusted agent ecosystems in the Internet of Agents.
tldr: The paper proposes a hierarchical, distributed trust discovery architecture for a future 'Internet of Agents', combining a registry-suffix-anchored composite identity scheme with dual-certificate authentication to enable scalable agent registration and capability discovery.
motivation: Autonomous agents across heterogeneous platforms need to register, identify, and discover each other reliably, but existing agent protocols focus only on tool invocation and messaging, leaving registration, trustworthy identification, and capability-oriented discovery unresolved at scale.
method: The authors design a three-layer architecture (Agent Root, Agent Registry, Agent Resolver) with composite identities binding native agent identifiers to trusted registry suffixes, plus dual-certificate and multi-level authentication, implemented as a prototype and evaluated with large-scale registration and resolution experiments.
result: The prototype achieves ~58 ms average registration latency and ~25 ms discovery latency, sustaining over 19,000 registration requests per second and over 29,000 discovery requests per second.
conclusion: The results suggest the architecture is feasible for scalable, identity-trusted agent ecosystems, though the work lies entirely in distributed systems and networking for AI agents with no connection to quantum information science.

title: Silence Is Endorsement: Verification-Status Laundering In Llm Agent Pipelines
authors: Yibo Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety monitors in LLM agent systems often judge actions from summaries or stored handoffs, not from the original evidence. This creates a simple but dangerous failure mode: the handoff preserves the claim that an action is authorized while losing the fact that the claim was never verified. We call this verification-status laundering. Across nine open-weight monitors and two hosted models, the action and authorization proposition remain fixed while we remove the unverified provenance framing around the claim. This change raises approval for risky actions from [MATH] to [MATH] on Llama-3.1-8B and from [MATH] to [MATH] on Qwen2.5-14B, with similarly large shifts on both hosted models. The failure also emerges in ordinary agent pipelines. Summarizers frequently weaken the status, memory compressors often remove it, and a full proposer--summarizer--memory--monitor pipeline raises risky approval to [MATH]--[MATH] across three downstream monitors. Experiments on WildGuard and ATBench show the same pattern on independently authored harmful and unsafe requests: unsupported authorization claims make approval substantially more likely. Explicitly instructing monitors to reject unverified authorization is not a reliable cross-model fix: some models remain vulnerable, while others reject legitimate requests. Agent systems should therefore carry authorization provenance as structured state attached to the claim throughout the pipeline.
tldr: The paper identifies a failure mode in LLM agent safety pipelines where verification status is lost during handoffs, causing monitors to approve risky actions more often.
motivation: Safety monitors often judge actions from summaries or stored handoffs rather than original evidence, which can drop the fact that an authorization claim was never verified.
method: Across nine open-weight monitors and two hosted models, the authors remove unverified provenance framing while keeping the action and authorization proposition fixed, then test on WildGuard and ATBench and in a full proposer-summarizer-memory-monitor pipeline.
result: Removing provenance raises approval for risky actions on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B, with similar large shifts on hosted models; explicit instructions to reject unverified authorization are not a reliable cross-model fix.
conclusion: Agent systems should carry authorization provenance as structured state attached to claims throughout the pipeline to prevent verification-status laundering.

title: Mollified-sharp Decomposition: A Probabilistic Regularization Of Parametric Pod For Shock-bearing Flows
authors: Oliver T. Schmidt
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the mollified-sharp decomposition, a probabilistic regularization of moving shocks in parametric reduced-order models. Each detected shock location is treated as a random variable with a prescribed probability density. Averaging over this artificial distribution replaces the localized pressure change by a smooth transition whose spatial extent is set by the density width, rather than by direct filtering of the pressure field. Each snapshot is decomposed exactly into a regularized mollified field and a local sharp correction that restores the shock. This probabilistic construction and exact additive split define the general method; the detector, kernel, treatment of multiple shocks, alignment coordinates, and regression are implementation choices. In the present realization, a calibrated indicator detects shocks, a compactly supported Wendland kernel mollifies them, and a peak-normalized and, where necessary, partitioned weight derived from each shock-location probability density defines the centroid, principal axes, and scales of its local alignment domain. Separate POD-GPR models represent the mollified field and aligned corrections, with additional regressions for shock presence and alignment. The method is demonstrated on the transonic airfoil pressure data of Catalani et al. (2023) and compared with a standard POD-GPR model constructed from the same data and POD-energy criterion. The mollified-sharp model reduces the mean test-set relative [MATH] pressure error by 31.2% and the mean test-set surface-pressure-coefficient error by 33.2%, while also improving the predicted shock locations and pressure changes; the trade-off is a median online evaluation time 2.24 times as long. The construction is applicable in principle to other parameter-dependent fields with moving sharp features, such as moving material interfaces in multiphase flows.
tldr: The paper introduces a mollified-sharp decomposition that probabilistically regularizes moving shocks in parametric reduced-order models (POD-GPR), improving airfoil pressure prediction accuracy at the cost of slower online evaluation.
motivation: Parametric reduced-order models struggle with moving sharp features such as shocks, because localized discontinuities are not well captured by standard low-rank decompositions.
method: Each detected shock location is treated as a random variable with a prescribed probability density; snapshots are then split exactly into a smoothed (mollified) field via a Wendland kernel and a local sharp correction, with separate POD-GPR regressions for the mollified field, aligned corrections, shock presence, and alignment.
result: On transonic airfoil pressure data the model reduces mean test-set relative pressure error by 31.2% and surface-pressure-coefficient error by 33.2%, while median online evaluation time increases by a factor of 2.24.
conclusion: The construction is a general probabilistic regularization applicable in principle to other parameter-dependent fields with moving sharp features, such as moving material interfaces in multiphase flows.

title: Geography As The Organizing Grammar Of Geospatial Models
authors: Shashank Tamaskar Rajiv Ranjan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GeoAI increasingly produces reusable Earth representation s, physical forecasts, multimodal systems, and reasoning a gents. Their progress exposes two distinct limitations. Geo graphic completeness asks whether the represented world ex tends beyond readily observed land surfaces and atmospher ic fields to oceans, biogeography, economies, institutions, and human agency. Geographic intelligence asks whether model outputs preserve place, scale, relations, process, un certainty, and the limits of valid inference. The first con cerns what exists in a model; the second concerns what may responsibly be claimed about it. This critical integrative review argues that geography provides the organizing gram mar that connects these dimensions. Seven structural gaps, propositions, and corresponding review questions translate the argument into testable requirements. The resulting re search agenda advances Living Geospatial Models as federat ed, continually updated systems that couple specialist Earth and human-domain models through shared geographic iden tity, support, relations, provenance, and uncertainty. The objective is not a single universal network, but geospatial intelligence that can explain connections and change, antic ipate plausible futures, and support accountable decisions across places and scales.
tldr: A critical integrative review arguing that geography should serve as the organizing grammar for geospatial AI models, proposing 'Living Geospatial Models' and seven structural gaps as a research agenda.
motivation: GeoAI has rapidly produced reusable Earth representations, forecasts, and reasoning agents, but progress exposes gaps in 'geographic completeness' (what the model represents) and 'geographic intelligence' (what can responsibly be claimed from outputs).
method: Conceptual critical integrative review that translates the argument into seven structural gaps, propositions, and corresponding review questions framed as testable requirements.
result: The review yields a research agenda for federated, continually updated 'Living Geospatial Models' that couple Earth and human-domain models through shared geographic identity, support, relations, provenance, and uncertainty.
conclusion: The objective is not a single universal network but geospatial intelligence capable of explaining connections and change, anticipating plausible futures, and supporting accountable decisions across places and scales.

title: NomadBBO: A Direct-search Framework For Constrained Mixed-variable Blackbox Optimization In Python
authors: Christophe Tribes Edward Hall\'e-Hannan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-variable blackbox optimization arises in simulation-based engineering and machine learning, where objective and constraint functions are expensive to evaluate and variables may be continuous, integer, binary, or categorical. Several software libraries are available for derivative-free optimization, but few combine ease of use, computational efficiency, flexibility, and theoretical convergence guarantees. This work presents NomadBBO, a user-friendly Python library for inequality-constrained mixed-variable blackbox optimization built around Nomad. Its core optimization framework is CatADS, a new direct-search method that extends Adaptive Direct Search (ADS) to mixed-variable problems. CatADS combines the mechanisms of ADS for quantitative variables with neighborhoods for handling categorical variables. These neighborhoods use Gaussian process-based or empirical Wasserstein distances derived from available data. Inequality constraints are handled through the progressive barrier. The mixed-variable and surrogate-based mechanisms are implemented in Python and connected to the efficient C++ backend of Nomad via Cython. This integration allows Nomad to handle categorical variables. It also enables the use of external libraries and hybrid optimization strategies, including Gaussian process models from SMT 2.0 and Bayesian optimization. Numerical experiments compare NomadBBO with other solvers on constrained and unconstrained mixed-variable problems from the Cat-Suite benchmark collection. The beta release is available at [URL].
tldr: NomadBBO is a Python library for inequality-constrained mixed-variable blackbox optimization, built on a new direct-search method called CatADS that extends Adaptive Direct Search to categorical variables using distance-based neighborhoods and handles constraints via a progressive barrier.
motivation: Mixed-variable blackbox optimization is common in simulation-based engineering and machine learning, but existing derivative-free optimization libraries rarely combine ease of use, efficiency, flexibility, and convergence guarantees.
method: The framework mixes ADS mechanisms for quantitative variables with Gaussian process-based or empirical Wasserstein distance neighborhoods for categorical variables, implements inequality constraints through a progressive barrier, and connects Python and C++ via Cython.
result: Numerical experiments on the Cat-Suite benchmark compare NomadBBO with other solvers on constrained and unconstrained mixed-variable problems, demonstrating its capabilities and integration with external libraries such as SMT 2.0 and Bayesian optimization.
conclusion: NomadBBO provides a user-friendly and theoretically grounded tool for practical constrained mixed-variable blackbox optimization, with a beta release available.

title: Wideband Directional $\mathcal{H}^2$-Matrix Compression For The Electric Field Integral Equation With Geometry-Adaptive Cluster Trees
authors: Simon B. Adrian Joshua M. Tetzner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an efficient wideband construction of directional [MATH]-matrices for the electrical field integral equation that, in contrast to existing constructions, supports not only box trees but also geometry-adaptive cluster trees. To accommodate geometry-adaptive cluster trees, we determine the number of directions from the electrical size of each cluster (instead of the level of a box tree), construct the directions using Spherical-Fibonacci points, and establish a hierarchy between the direction sets of a cluster and its children through an angular nearest-neighbor mapping. We construct the nested directional representation using the incomplete adaptive cross approximation, for which we introduce a robustified tree-mimicry pivoting strategy that prevents premature convergence for block-structured matrices arising from certain geometries and meshes. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves the desired accuracy, requires no more storage than the octree-based construction and substantially less when the geometry or discretization is poorly matched to octree clustering, and exhibits the expected [MATH] scaling for high-frequency problems.
tldr: The paper presents a wideband directional H^2-matrix compression scheme for the electric field integral equation that supports geometry-adaptive cluster trees rather than only box/octree structures.
motivation: Existing wideband directional H^2-matrix constructions are restricted to box trees, which causes inefficiency when the geometry or discretization is poorly matched to octree clustering, motivating a more flexible, geometry-adaptive approach.
method: The authors determine direction counts from each cluster's electrical size, generate directions via Spherical-Fibonacci points, link parent-child direction sets through angular nearest-neighbor mapping, and build the nested representation using incomplete adaptive cross approximation with a robustified tree-mimicry pivoting strategy.
result: Numerical experiments show the approach meets target accuracy, uses no more storage than octree-based constructions (and substantially less for poorly matched geometries), and exhibits the expected complexity scaling for high-frequency problems.
conclusion: The method generalizes wideband directional H^2-matrix compression to geometry-adaptive cluster trees, improving efficiency for challenging geometries while retaining accuracy and asymptotic scaling.

title: Where The Llm Ends And Reliable Decisions Begin
authors: Priyadarshan Patil, Abhishek Basu, Vikas Reddy, Abhinav Gupta
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems that turn natural-language descriptions of optimization problems into solver-ready code generally use a language model at every stage, including the final translation from a mathematical formulation into executable model-building code. We propose the ANVIL compiler architecture, where we separate these concerns. A language model is called only once, assisted by constraint guidance based on problem type, to produce a LaTeX formulation. A deterministic compiler then translates that LaTeX into code with no language model involvement. We describe the deterministic compiler (a normalizer, a recursive-descent parser producing a typed intermediate representation, analysis passes that bind symbols to a dataset schema, and a code emitter) and evaluate it on the 354 easy and hard problems of the NLP4LP benchmark. The compiler produced code for 329 of 354 formulations (92.9%), taking the deterministic path in every one of those cases and never falling back to model-generated code. Median compile time was below the 10ms resolution of our timer. Overall, our formulations achieved an accuracy of 98.9% over easy problems and 91.1% for hard problems. The gap between these compilation and accuracy figures is a key point of analysis, and we analyze it: formulations that failed to compile, problems that returned as infeasible, problems raising errors at runtime, and problems returning a wrong objective. Almost all of these errors trace back to the formulation rather than to the translation. ANVIL performs exceptionally well on leading benchmarks by using language models purely where they are effective, rather than as a catch-all tool.
tldr: The ANVIL compiler architecture uses a single language model call to produce a LaTeX formulation of optimization problems, then a deterministic compiler translates that LaTeX into solver-ready code, achieving high compilation and accuracy rates on the NLP4LP benchmark.
motivation: Existing systems that convert natural-language optimization problems into solver code invoke LLMs at every stage, including the final code translation, which introduces unnecessary unreliability. The authors aim to confine LLM usage to where it is effective—semantic formulation—and delegate the mechanical translation to deterministic software.
method: A language model, aided by constraint guidance conditioned on problem type, generates only a LaTeX formulation of the optimization problem; a deterministic compiler (normalizer, recursive-descent parser producing a typed IR, schema-binding analysis passes, and a code emitter) then converts this LaTeX into executable model-building code without any further model involvement.
result: The compiler generated code for 329 of 354 NLP4LP problems (92.9%) entirely through the deterministic path, with median compile time below the timer's 10 ms resolution, and the resulting formulations scored 98.9% accuracy on easy problems and 91.1% on hard problems, with nearly all residual errors traced to the formulation rather than translation.
conclusion: Separating LLM-based formulation from deterministic compilation yields reliable, fast, and accurate solver-code generation, showing that language models are best used selectively rather than as a catch-all component in optimization workflows.

title: Local Matrix Muckenhoupt Weights And Quantitative Weighted Inequalities Achieving Global Best Known Exponents
authors: Tuomas Hyt\"onen, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Mingdong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we give various real-variable properties of local Muckenhoupt matrix weights [MATH] and establish the quantitative boundedness of several operators on local matrix-weighted Lebesgue spaces [MATH], including local (fractional) maximal operators, local fractional integral operators, local Haar square functions, and Calder\'{o}n--Zygmund operators with exponential decay. For the local maximal operators, we obtain the sharp quantitative bounds when [MATH], while, for local fractional integral operators, we obtain the quantitative bounds matching the global best known exponents, whose scalar case is known to be sharp. The key used strategies include giving a new extension property (which can clarify their relationships with global ones) and an optimal scale lifting property (which can balance the locality of weights and operators under consideration) of local matrix weights. As an application, we establish the quantitative boundedness on [MATH] of the Riesz transform associated with Schr\"{o}dinger operators [MATH] with [MATH] being large enough, whose quantitative bound when [MATH] is precisely [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies local matrix Muckenhoupt weights and establishes quantitative boundedness of local maximal, fractional integral, square function, and Calderón--Zygmund operators with sharp or globally optimal exponents.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a local matrix-weighted theory that parallels classical Muckenhoupt weight theory while allowing locality and matrix-valued weights, and to obtain quantitative bounds matching the global best known exponents.
method: They prove real-variable properties of local matrix Muckenhoupt weights, including a new extension property relating local and global weights and an optimal scale lifting property, then use these to bound several operators on local matrix-weighted Lebesgue spaces.
result: Sharp quantitative bounds are obtained for local maximal operators when p=1, and for local fractional integral operators the bounds match the global best known exponents; as an application, quantitative boundedness of Riesz transforms for Schrödinger operators is established.
conclusion: The work extends weighted harmonic analysis to the local matrix-weighted setting and provides sharp or best-known quantitative estimates with applications to Schrödinger operator Riesz transforms.

title: Epidemic Control Using Stackelberg Mean Field Game With Budget Constraint
authors: Gokce Dayanikli Huaning Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Epidemic mitigation comes with a price in practice, and when budget is limited, its effective allocation becomes an important question on public policy. In this paper, we study epidemic control through a Stackelberg mean-field game in which a principal, representing the government, chooses social distancing guidelines and vaccination levels for a large population of rational minor agents subject to a budget-spending process. The principal anticipates the minor agents mean-field Nash equilibrium (MFNE) and selects intervention policies to minimize her own objective, inducing a bi-level optimal control problem. We define the Stackelberg mean-field game equilibrium (SMFE) and give its necessary condition by a forward-backward ordinary differential equation (FBODE) system, and provide existence and uniqueness results. We further propose an iterative fixed-point algorithm to solve the FBODE numerically and present computational observations that illustrate the resulting equilibrium behavior.
tldr: The paper formulates epidemic control as a Stackelberg mean-field game where a government principal sets social distancing and vaccination policies for a large population of rational agents under a budget constraint.
motivation: Epidemic mitigation is costly, and limited public budgets make optimal allocation of interventions a key policy question that requires balancing government objectives against individuals' rational behavioral responses.
method: The authors define a Stackelberg mean-field game equilibrium (SMFE), derive its necessary conditions as a forward-backward ordinary differential equation (FBODE) system with existence and uniqueness results, and propose an iterative fixed-point algorithm for numerical solution.
result: Existence and uniqueness of the SMFE are established, and computational observations illustrate the equilibrium behavior arising from the budget-constrained intervention policies.
conclusion: The framework offers a principled mean-field game approach to designing cost-aware epidemic interventions that anticipate the population's Nash equilibrium response.

title: (Cheap) Stochastic Policy Gradient Converges With High Probability For Linear Quadratic Regulator
authors: Chengze Xie Yan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the convergence of the vanilla stochastic policy gradient method applied to the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem. The method is cheap in the following sense: (1) at each iteration only [MATH] interactions with the environment are needed, therefore allowing frequent policy improvement steps, and (2) to ensure stability throughout and convergence to an [MATH]-optimal policy with probability [MATH], only [MATH] interactions are needed. To the best of our knowledge, this appears to be the first time that a stochastic model-free policy optimization method for LQR converges with high probability with [MATH] per-iteration computation and polylogarithmic dependence on the confidence level. The convergence analysis presented here is agnostic to LQR specifics and hence could be potentially generalized to a broader class of problems.
tldr: The paper proves that vanilla stochastic policy gradient for the linear quadratic regulator converges to an ε-optimal policy with high probability using only O(1) environment interactions per iteration and polylogarithmic dependence on the confidence level.
motivation: Model-free policy optimization for LQR is widely used but its convergence guarantees—especially high-probability bounds with cheap per-iteration sampling—remain incomplete.
method: The authors analyze the vanilla stochastic policy gradient algorithm, exploiting structural properties of the LQR cost to control gradient estimation error and stability, and prove a high-probability convergence guarantee.
result: They obtain the first high-probability convergence result for stochastic model-free policy optimization on LQR with per-iteration computation of order M and polylogarithmic dependence on the confidence level, requiring only O(·) total interactions for stability and ε-optimality.
conclusion: The analysis is agnostic to LQR specifics and may generalize to broader classes of stochastic control and reinforcement learning problems.

title: Extended MF-AFBSDDEswCN And Stochastic Optimal Controls Of Linear System
authors: Hao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The research studies the extended mean-field anticipated forward-backward stochastic delayed differential equations with common noise (extended MF-AFBSDDEswCN) by expanding the domination-monotonicity conditions. We generalize the conditions from a linear setting to a nonlinear one by including nonlinear adjoint functions which are key to guaranteeing the well-posedness of extended MF-AFBSDDEswCN. Utilizing this broader well-posedness framework for extended MF-AFBSDDEswCN, combined with other refined analytical tools, we examine two classes of stochastic optimal control problems. These include a linear-convex problem and a linear-quadratic problem with input constraints that can be both time-dependent and random. Moreover, the control elements regarding the initial values are path-dependent, which will cause some essential difficulties. For each problem, we establish the existence and uniqueness of optimal controls and provide their explicit, closed-form representations.
tags: anticipated delayed equations with common noise
tldr: The paper extends well-posedness conditions for mean-field anticipated forward-backward stochastic delayed differential equations with common noise (MF-AFBSDDEswCN) and applies them to solve linear-convex and linear-quadratic stochastic optimal control problems with path-dependent, possibly random input constraints.
motivation: Existing domination-monotonicity conditions guaranteeing well-posedness of MF-AFBSDDEswCN were limited to a linear setting, restricting the class of solvable stochastic optimal control problems with delays, anticipation, and common noise.
method: The authors generalize the domination-monotonicity conditions to a nonlinear regime by introducing nonlinear adjoint functions, establish well-posedness of the extended equations, and then combine this with refined analytical tools to treat two classes of stochastic optimal control problems.
result: For both the linear-convex problem and the linear-quadratic problem with time-dependent and random input constraints, existence and uniqueness of the optimal control are proved and explicit closed-form representations are derived.
conclusion: The broader well-posedness framework for extended MF-AFBSDDEswCN enables closed-form solutions to constrained stochastic optimal control problems with path-dependent initial data, though the work remains entirely within classical stochastic analysis and control theory.
keywords: anticipated delayed equations with common noise

title: Pairwise Comparisons Meet Optimal Transport Theory
authors: Silvia Lorenzini Matteo Brunelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we reinterpret pairwise comparison theory through the lens of optimal transport. The main contribution is the connection established between pairwise comparison matrices, doubly stochastic scaling, and entropy-regularized transport problems. Using Sinkhorn scaling, we show how consistency, priority derivation, and inconsistency assessment can be studied within a common optimal-transport framework. As methodological consequences of this connection, we obtain a new characterization of consistency, a Sinkhorn-based prioritization method, and an entropy-based inconsistency index. We study these proposals both analytically and numerically and compare them with established methods from the literature.
tldr: The paper connects pairwise comparison matrices to entropy-regularized optimal transport via Sinkhorn scaling, yielding new consistency characterization and prioritization/inconsistency methods.
motivation: Pairwise comparisons are central to multi-criteria decision making, but lack a unifying framework with modern transport and entropy-based tools.
method: Reinterprets pairwise comparison theory through optimal transport, linking matrices to doubly stochastic scaling and entropy-regularized transport, and uses Sinkhorn scaling for analysis and computation.
result: Provides a new consistency characterization, a Sinkhorn-based prioritization method, and an entropy-based inconsistency index, with analytical and numerical comparisons to established methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that optimal transport offers a coherent lens for consistency, priority derivation, and inconsistency assessment in pairwise comparisons.

title: Optimal Estimation And Goodness-of-fit Testing Of The Mean For Sparse Longitudinal Functional Data
authors: Mahdi Saidi Valentin Patilea
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the mean function of longitudinal functional data, where each subject contributes a small number of complete profiles over a general domain, observed at random visit times. The mean is projected onto an orthonormal basis in the time direction, and each coefficient function is estimated by a weighted average of the profiles. We consider deterministic and random weights, including closed-form, data-driven weights that dispense with the design density entirely. For each weighting scheme we derive non-asymptotic bounds on the integrated quadratic risk and an explicit optimal truncation level. All schemes share the same convergence rate, which we show to be minimax optimal over the corresponding coefficient-decay class, only the leading constants differ. We also provide a goodness-of-fit test for the mean function, and derive non-asymptotic bounds for the Gaussian approximation of its distribution under both the null and alternative hypotheses. Our estimation and testing procedures are easy to implement, fast, and perform well in applications.
tldr: The paper develops optimal estimation and goodness-of-fit testing for the mean function of sparse longitudinal functional data.
motivation: Longitudinal functional data often feature subjects with few observed profiles at random times, requiring robust methods for mean estimation and hypothesis testing.
method: The mean is projected onto an orthonormal basis in time, with coefficient functions estimated via weighted averages using deterministic, random, and data-driven weights; non-asymptotic risk bounds and an optimal truncation level are derived, alongside a goodness-of-fit test.
result: All weighting schemes achieve the same minimax optimal convergence rate over coefficient-decay classes, with only leading constants differing, and the test's Gaussian approximation is bounded under null and alternative hypotheses.
conclusion: The proposed procedures are computationally efficient, perform well in applications, and provide theoretical guarantees for sparse longitudinal functional data analysis.

title: EvoSherlock: Towards Agentic Lifelong Evolution For Unseen Long-Tailed Security-Critical Events In Videos
authors: Zixin Fan, Jiahong Lu, Changsheng Zheng, Yu Hong, Jingjing Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing Security-oriented Video Understanding (SVU) systems assume a , \ie static category sets, abundant labels, and the premise that all event types are known upfront. Real-world security-critical events break these assumptions: they follow long-tailed distributions, new types emerge continuously, and critical security events may offer only a few samples. We formalize this gap as -SCE)}, a new task that requires VLMs to continually classify and temporally localize newly emerging security-critical events from scarce samples without forgetting previously learned events. Furthermore, \task reveals two critical challenges: (1)~, where extreme data scarcity may weaken both classification and temporal localization for new events, and (2)~, where cross-event feature entanglement and representation drift may strengthen catastrophic forgetting. On this basis, we propose , a causal-enhanced approach orchestrated end-to-end by an with self-reflective closed-loop control, which includes two core modules: the Intra-Event ausal ideo eneration module () and the Inter-Event ausal ecoupling and lignment module (), to address the above two challenges, respectively. Especially, this paper constructs a \task dataset to simulate real-world incremental conditions. Extensive experiments on our benchmark demonstrate the advantages of \method over several advanced baselines. These justify the importance of the proposed \task and the effectiveness of \method in classifying and temporally localizing emerging security-critical events from scarce samples.
tldr: EvoSherlock proposes an agentic lifelong-learning framework with causal video generation and causal decoupling modules to classify and temporally localize newly emerging, long-tailed security-critical events in videos from scarce samples without catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Existing security-oriented video understanding systems assume static category sets, abundant labels, and full prior knowledge of event types, which fails in real-world settings where security-critical events are long-tailed, continuously emerging, and sample-scarce.
method: The authors formalize the Streaming/Incremental Security-Critical Event (SCE) task and introduce EvoSherlock, an end-to-end agent-orchestrated approach with self-reflective closed-loop control, comprising an Intra-Event Causal Video Generation module and an Inter-Event Causal Decoupling and Alignment module, along with a purpose-built benchmark dataset.
result: Extensive experiments on the constructed benchmark show EvoSherlock outperforms several advanced baselines in classifying and temporally localizing emerging security-critical events from scarce samples.
conclusion: The paper argues for the importance of the new streaming SCE task and demonstrates the effectiveness of causal-enhanced agentic lifelong evolution for video-based security event understanding.

title: Asymptotic Max-Min Fair Allocation With Random Utilities
authors: Amir Leshem Noam Glazner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.19319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the asymptotic behavior of max-min fair allocations for indivisible goods under i.i.d. random utilities. For [MATH] agents and [MATH] goods with utilities [MATH] drawn independently from a common distribution [MATH], we derive asymptotic characterizations of the max-min value in the balanced case [MATH] (and in [MATH] extensions) via distributional quantiles. We then study the efficiency impact of max-min fairness by comparing the resulting total welfare with the optimal sum welfare. For distributions with sufficiently light tails, we prove that the relative efficiency loss converges to zero as the market grows, implying that max-min fairness incurs negligible welfare loss in large random instances for a broad class of distributions.
tldr: The paper derives asymptotic characterizations of max-min fair allocations for indivisible goods with i.i.d. random utilities and shows the welfare loss from fairness vanishes in large markets with light-tailed distributions.
